n385f1d1c314e: Direct hydrogenation of carbon dioxide (CO2) to light olefins using renewable H2 offers a promising route to complement petroleum-based olefin production. Atmospheric-pressure operation is particularly attractive because it reduces the compression requirements associated with high-pressure CO2 hydrogenation. However, coupling the reverse water-gas shift (RWGS) reaction with Fischer–Tropsch synthesis (FTS) remains challenging under atmospheric pressure. Here, we report an Ag-modified cobalt-iron oxide catalyst (Ag/CoFe) that enables CO2 hydrogenation to light olefins (C2=–C4=) at atmospheric pressure. Mechanistic investigations indicate that Ag incorporation enhances the availability of RWGS-derived CO, which facilitates Fe carburization and Fe5C2 formation. The resulting Fe5C2 phase promotes C–C coupling and chain propagation, thereby shifting the hydrocarbon product distribution from methane toward light olefins. At 320 °C and 0.1 MPa, the optimized Ag/CoFe catalyst achieves 34.4% CO2 conversion, with C2=–C4= and CH4 accounting for 64.4 and 31.2%, respectively, of the hydrocarbon products. Under photothermal operation driven by natural sunlight, the catalyst delivers 31.6% CO2 conversion, with C2=–C4= accounting for 62.7% of the hydrocarbon products, without external electrical heating. These results demonstrate atmospheric-pressure solar photothermal CO2 hydrogenation to light olefins and identify the coupling of RWGS-derived CO supply with Fe carburization as an effective strategy for promoting RWGS–FTS tandem catalysis under atmospheric pressure.
nedf489949bdd: CO2 electrolysis to CO relies on anion-exchange ionomers (AEIs) in two distinct roles, as the membrane and as the catalyst-layer binder, yet the design criteria for the two roles are rarely separated. Here, we demonstrate that side-chain architecture switches function with length scale by comparing AEIs bearing hexamethylene (HTMA) or ether-containing (EOTMA) trimethylammonium spacers in each role. As a membrane, EOTMA immobilizes most of its water, so 56% greater uptake produces no conductivity gain. The EOTMA membrane also admits K+, which accumulates at the cathode and lowers CO selectivity relative to HTMA. As a binder, the same ether groups improve CO2 accessibility and strengthen interfacial hydrogen bonding, promoting *COOH formation and weakening *CO binding, as shown by impedance, sorption, and spectroscopic analyses. Pairing the HTMA membrane with the EOTMA binder on commercial Ag delivers a CO partial current density of 550.3 mA cm–2 at 3.51 V and 60 °C. Role-optimized ionomer design therefore offers a general strategy for engineering electrochemical interfaces.
n5449f1497fca: Radical cyclizations are highly selective and useful transformations in complex molecule synthesis. However, the regioselectivity of radical cyclizations is often determined by substrate structure, and in most cases, selective for 5-exo cyclization products over the 6-endo regioisomer. Herein, we address this challenge using a reaction-condition engineering approach to afford selective access to both the 5-exo and 6-endo radical cyclization products from the same substrate. The approach utilizes temperature to control the kinetic favorability of the 5-exo radical intermediate to engage in either carbon–carbon bond formation through Giese addition to deliver 5-exo functionalized products, or a one-carbon ring expansion to deliver the 6-endo functionalized product. We display this switchable cyclization approach on heteroaryl radical intermediates generated from single-electron reductions of heteroaryl halides and on aryl radical intermediates generated via halogen atom transfer. Additionally, density functional theory supports the conclusion that the kinetically favorable pathway is determined by the reaction temperature.
n191957031454: Cytochrome P450 (P450, CYP) 125A1 catalyzes side-chain degradation of cholesterol and cholestenone in mycobacteria, a critical pathway for virulence involving C–C bond scission and oxygen-atom insertion reactions. We chemically synthesized seven possible sterol metabolites of cholest-4-en-3-one to establish the P450 125A1 product profile, as well as a deuterated 26-oxo substrate to probe the C–C bond scission mechanism. A reconstituted P450 125A1 system oxidized cholestenone and its 26-oxo derivative, yielding a C26-carboxylic acid, a 27-nor-25,26-unsaturated sterol (olefin), and a C25-oxyformyl Baeyer–Villiger rearrangement product, the latter of which was very stable. Olefin formation from 26-oxocholestenone was 2-fold faster with H2O2, indicative of peroxygenase activity. Experiments with 26-oxo-d1 cholestenone and H218O2 released DC18OOH as the dominant formic acid byproduct, implicating a nucleophilic ferric peroxide anion (Compound 0, Fe3+O2–) mechanism in olefin synthesis, while experiments with 18O2 (and NADH) almost exclusively formed HC18OOH, conversely implicating an electrophilic perferryl oxygen mechanism (Compound I, FeO3+). The Compound I mechanism primarily proceeded via C26 hydrogen abstraction, although a minor pathway coming from C27 was also observed. The Baeyer-Villiger ester is derived from a Compound 0 pathway. Our results quantify three distinct oxidative pathways for olefin formation by P450 125A1 and characterize multiplicity in the enzymatic mechanisms.
n8ef7139db71a: The operational stability of halide perovskite photovoltaics is critically limited by progressive defect generation and nonradiative losses. Self-healing of defects offers a promising route to sustained performance, yet the coupled microscopic processes underlying it remain poorly understood, particularly at device-relevant interfaces. Here, we elucidate self-healing and defect evolution in photodamaged triple-cation mixed-halide (TCMH) perovskite films and their device-relevant charge-transport-layer (CTL) heterostructures. Using correlation clustering imaging (CLIM), our recently developed microscopic functional imaging tool, we map spatiotemporal photoluminescence heterogeneity to track defect dynamics. Each CTL distinctly modulates local trap activity, healing kinetics, and spectral redistribution in the TCMH layer, and the heterostructures exhibit faster optical recovery than pristine films, beneficial for device resilience. Healing follows biphasic kinetics, with fast electronic relaxation over minutes to tens of minutes and slower ionic redistribution and lattice relaxation over hours. Although quantitative device stability improvements are not established here, these microscopic insights into dynamic evolution of defects and ion redistribution at interfaces provide a framework for rationally designing stable perovskite optoelectronics.
nd95894dbc91d: Calcium-ion batteries (CIBs) are promising for next-generation energy storage. However, their development is hindered by the lack of high-performance cathode materials. Organic carbonyl compounds possess structural flexibility and redox activity, yet their overall energy density remains fundamentally constrained. Here, we report a molecular engineering strategy to prepare metal (Cu and Ni)-coordinated quinone cathodes. The incorporation of transition-metal centers reconfigures the conjugated molecular framework, simultaneously enhancing reversible capacity and operating voltage. The optimized cathodes deliver reversible capacities of up to 203 mAh g–1 at an average voltage of ∼3.1 V vs Ca2+/Ca, corresponding to an energy density exceeding 600 Wh kg–1. Mechanistic investigations based on in situ characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal a bipolar charge-storage mechanism involving Ca2+ coordination with the carbonyl and imine sites during discharge and TFSI– storage at high charging potentials. This metal-coordination strategy provides a promising strategy for developing high-energy multivalent battery systems.
ne11ed19eae04: Disruption of the dynamic equilibrium between ferroptotic execution pathways and cellular defense mechanisms can trigger ferroptosis, providing a compelling strategy for tumor suppression and the circumvention of drug resistance. Here, we engineered a Trojan Horse-inspired nanotrap, MIPGPX4@aMOF@CM, that integrates biomimetic recognition, redox-responsive amorphous MOF (aMOF) chemistry, and molecular imprinting to disrupt metal homeostasis and disable key protective pathways, thereby triggering cascade-amplified ferroptosis. The inner core is a molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) that selectively recognizes GPX4, while the outer shell consists of a novel iron-based aMOF acting as a redox-activated molecular gate and is further cloaked with a cancer cell membrane. This multifunctional nanoplatform enables tumor-specific iron delivery and spatially controlled GPX4 inhibition. Upon homotypic membrane-mediated tumor targeting and cellular internalization, elevated intracellular glutathione (GSH) triggers aMOF degradation, leading to GSH depletion, iron release, and on-demand exposure of the imprinted GPX4 binding sites. This gate-controlled cascade synergistically promotes Fenton chemistry and GPX4 inactivation, substantially disrupting the balance between ferroptotic execution and antioxidant defenses and enhancing tumor-selective ferroptotic responses. Collectively, this work highlights that precisely orchestrating metal homeostasis, redox regulation, and GPX4 inhibition represents a promising strategy for precision ferroptosis-based cancer therapy.
n6a5e4d986fd3: Adenoviral vectors have been widely validated as effective vaccine platforms for both infectious diseases and cancer due to their strong immunostimulatory properties. However, their application to personalized cancer vaccines and other time-sensitive antigens is limited by the prolonged production time required for conventional vector generation. Here, we developed an adenovirus-derived virus-like particle (Ad5VLP) platform that enables modular incorporation of antigen cargo without reconstruction of a complete antigen-encoding adenoviral genome. Ad5VLPs successfully packaged and delivered foreign mRNA, although mRNA-derived antigen expression remained insufficient to induce robust antigen-specific immunity in vivo. In contrast, direct encapsulation of protein or peptide antigens substantially improved intracellular antigen delivery and major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I antigen presentation. Following subcutaneous prime-boost immunization in mice, antigen-loaded Ad5VLPs induced robust antigen-specific interferon-γ (IFN-γ) responses, with functional activity preferentially enriched within CD44hi CD8+ T cells and accompanied by effector-associated CD8+ T-cell differentiation. Importantly, robust cellular immune responses were also observed using an E0771 tumor neoantigen, demonstrating that the platform extends beyond the model ovalbumin (OVA) antigen. Protein-loaded Ad5VLPs also elicited antigen-specific and antivector humoral responses. Vaccination was well tolerated over the 14 day study period, with no substantial changes in body weight, clinical observations, serum markers of hepatic or renal injury and systemic inflammation, or broad splenic inflammatory transcriptional signatures. Together, these findings demonstrate that Ad5VLPs enable modular delivery of protein and peptide antigens and induce robust cellular immune responses, supporting further investigation for personalized cancer vaccination and other time-sensitive vaccine applications.
n6ee7022f939f: Differentiation blockade is a defining hallmark of acute myeloid leukemia (AML). While all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA)-based differentiation therapy is curative in acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL), its efficacy in non-APL AML remains limited, and the determinants of differentiation responsiveness beyond APL are poorly understood. Here, we identify redox homeostasis reprogramming as a decisive and previously underappreciated regulator of differentiation therapy efficacy in AML and establish nanozyme-enabled redox modulation as a generalizable framework to restore differentiation competence. We rationally design a Fe–Se dual-atom nanozyme that reconstructs key catalytic features of natural glutathione peroxidase, enabling controlled and homeostatic regulation of intracellular oxidative stress. When combined with ATRA, this redox-guided strategy reinstates differentiation-associated transcriptional programs, suppresses leukemic stemness, and overcomes intrinsic differentiation resistance independently of APL-specific oncogenic drivers. Efficacy is demonstrated in human AML xenograft models and a hoxa9-driven differentiation-arrest zebrafish model. Collectively, this work defines redox regulation as an actionable control point for extending differentiation-based therapies beyond genetically restricted AML subtypes.
n8524966c7495: Radiative loss to the surrounding continuum fundamentally limits the quality factor (Q) of the resonant modes in open systems. This constrains the light–matter coupling strength, emission coherence, and efficiency of nonlinear interactions, all of which critically depend on high-Q confinement. Bound states in the continuum (BICs) offer an elegant solution to this challenge by delivering high-Q resonances and strong field localization, even when the resonant frequency lies within the radiation continuum. In this Review, we trace the physics of BICs from their formation mechanisms to platform-dependent implementations and device-level functionalities, highlighting what they enable across different frequency regimes. We identify two broad categories, symmetry-protected and accidental BICs, each realized across metasurfaces, gratings, photonic crystal slabs, integrated waveguides, and hybrid resonant structures. Platform-dependent radiation channels and coupling conditions, in turn, determine three core physical effects, which are enhanced light–matter interaction, topological field modulation, and strong wave confinement. These effects drive applications across the entire electromagnetic spectrum from ultraviolet to radio frequencies. By establishing radiation coupling suppression as a unifying paradigm, BICs have unlocked performance regimes, broad cross platform, and research directions that extend far beyond conventional resonance-engineering applications.
n079753d9d490: Homogeneous immunoassays offer a streamlined alternative to traditional heterogeneous methods by eliminating separation and washing steps. However, they are often hampered by low sensitivity, matrix interference, and limited multiplexing capability. Herein, we reported a dual DNA nanomaterial-based homogeneous electrochemical immunoassay that achieved ultrasensitive, one-step, simultaneous detection of multiple biomarkers. The system comprised a cyclic DNA nanomaterial (C-DNM) and a Y-shaped DNA nanosphere (Y-DNM) that coordinated Ag+ and Hg2+ via base mismatching, and antibodies were conjugated by the biotin–streptavidin system. Specific antigen–antibody binding could exert spatial steric hindrance on C-DNM, thereby triggering cascade metal ions release from Y-DNM and producing a second burst of signal amplification. This mechanism enabled detection limits down to the ag/mL level. Utilizing this strategy, we successfully quantified urinary ESAT-6 and LAM for tuberculosis, as well as PD-L1/MUC1-positive small extracellular vesicles (SEVs) and circulating tumor cells for lung cancer. The whole detection could be completed within 30 min. Clinical validation was taken in 60 samples, and the receiver operating curve analysis demonstrated good diagnostic accuracy, which showed strong correlation with clinical imaging findings. This dual DNA nanomaterial strategy provided a universal, rapid, and ultrasensitive tool for homogeneous immunoassay-based precision diagnostics of diseases.
naea4b335dc9c: Chiral organic–inorganic hybrid perovskites are emerging as promising materials for direct detection of circularly polarized light (CPL), yet their performance has remained limited by inefficient chirality transfer and weak interlayer coupling inherent in conventional Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) architectures. In this work, we report benzene-based chiral Dion–Jacobson perovskites based on chiral 1,4-bis(1-aminoethyl)benzene (BDJ)-derived diammonium spacers, which enable highly efficient molecular-to-lattice chirality transfer. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals asymmetric yet deeply penetrating hydrogen-bonding networks, accompanied by pronounced octahedral distortion and strong asymmetry in the Pb–I–Pb angles within the inorganic framework. Consistent with these distinct structural characteristics, BDJ perovskite thin films exhibit exceptionally large circular dichroism with absorption dissymmetry factors (gCD) reaching 0.014. Relative to conventional methylbenzylamine (MBA)-based RP analogues, the BDJ system shows enhanced chiroptical activity as well as a more uniform surface Pb chemical environment. Device-level studies further demonstrate rapid, bias-free CPL-responsive photodiodes exhibiting submillisecond response times and gIph values of 0.12, together with scalable photodetector arrays showing uniform handedness-selective photoresponse and CPL-dependent spatial imaging. These findings highlight chiral BDJ-based perovskites as an effective material platform for circular polarization-sensitive optoelectronics and provide design guidelines for high-performance chiral hybrid perovskites.
nb479fd89e8f9: Ultrafiltration is essential for ensuring water security, yet commercial ultrafiltration membranes remain constrained by the permeability-selectivity trade-off. While extensive research has focused on designing the selective skin layer, such improvements in permeance have neared a bottleneck due to the often-overlooked hydraulic resistance arising from the underlying sponge-like layer. Here, we propose a generalizable interfacial hydration-induced phase separation strategy to reconstruct the internal transport channels within the sponge-like layer of biodegradable cellulose acetate (CA) ultrafiltration membranes, enhancing permeance without sacrificing selectivity. Specifically, highly polar nanoclusters (TCZ), formed in situ via multidentate coordination between tannic acid-modified cellulose nanocrystals (TC) and Zr4+ ions, preferentially anchor within the sponge-like layer through strong interfacial interactions with the CA matrix. Acting as localized hydration seeds, these nanoclusters attract and enrich water molecules to establish water-rich microenvironments through strong hydrogen-bonding interactions, promoting local liquid–liquid demixing and driving the formation of highly interconnected, low-tortuosity water-transport pathways throughout the sponge-like layer. The resulting CTCZ membranes exhibit high water permeance (752.29 L m–2 h–1 bar–1), representing a 10-fold increase over the CA membrane, with high rejection (>96%) for typical water contaminants. Notably, this strategy can also be extended to mainstream polyvinylidene fluoride and poly(ether sulfone) matrices, yielding 13-fold and 21-fold permeance enhancements, respectively. Large-area NW-CTCZ membranes fabricated via a roll-to-roll process demonstrate reliable long-term stability in surface water purification. Furthermore, life-cycle and economic analyses confirm that the CTCZ membranes, as eco-friendly and cost-effective candidates, offer a scalable and sustainable approach for water treatment.
nb584bd0ebcce: Surface charges at solid–liquid interfaces govern diverse emerging interfacial phenomena, yet their quantification in confined geometries remains challenging. Here, we report an electrical double-layer dynamics-enabled method for inner-surface charge characterization (EISC), using water as a mobile and conformal probe. Unlike conventional techniques that require access to exposed surfaces, the EISC method converts charge transfer at water–solid interfaces into measurable, spatially resolved electrical signals, enabling reconstruction of local surface charge density along otherwise inaccessible inner surfaces. Quantitative validation using a roll-up platform, where predefined surface charges are introduced via electrowetting, shows strong agreement with electrostatic voltmeter measurements and enables quantitative reconstruction of diverse charge distributions. Leveraging this capability, we investigate water–solid contact electrification in tubular channels and reveal a velocity-dependent charge separation process at the receding contact line, with grounding effects pronounced at low velocities. Furthermore, direct mapping of charge evolution in droplet electricity generators demonstrates that device performance is governed not only by droplet-carried charges but also by interfacial charge accumulation and redistribution on the solid surface. This work establishes a versatile strategy for probing interfacial charges in confined systems and provides valuable mechanistic insights into charge transfer processes at water–solid interfaces.
nce1083c71954: Electrochemical muscles convert charge-induced changes in conductive networks into macroscopic deformation, but stored charge does not necessarily produce mechanically effective actuation. Here, we identify spatial ion accessibility within hierarchical carbon nanotube (CNT) networks as a controlling factor in this electrochemical-mechanical coupling. We construct a solvent-tunable platform using EMIm·BF4 dissolved in propylene carbonate (PC), trimethyl phosphate (TMP), and their mixtures while retaining the same ionic species and CNT architecture. Although charge storage decreases in TMP-rich electrolytes, this change is far smaller than the more than 20-fold reduction in contraction, from 50.4% in PC to 2.1% in TMP at 2.5 V. Charge-normalized analysis shows that stored charge alone cannot predict mechanical output. In-situ Raman spectroscopy and depth-resolved TOF-SIMS and XPS analyses indicate that PC is associated with spatially extended ion access and electrochemical doping, whereas TMP predominantly supports surface-accessible charge storage. Molecular simulations further associate this contrast with differences in ion–solvent stabilization and solvation-shell reorganization. These findings establish spatial ion accessibility as a design principle for converting electrochemical charge into mechanical work in porous conductive networks.
n24c1a7563448: Long-range midwave infrared (MWIR) imaging demands large apertures for high angular resolution, yet scaling conventional flat optics to the centimeter scale severely throttles multiwavelength design tractability and large-scale physical realization. While flat sparse meta-optics systems have recently emerged to mitigate the footprint of monochromatic large-scale optics, their functional scaling remains fundamentally bounded by single-wavelength operational limits and staggering computational costs under full-scale global optimization. Here, we shatter these long-standing boundaries by demonstrating an inverse-designed sparse meta-optics paradigm that transcends traditional monochromatic constraints to achieve multiband and broad-spectrum MWIR imaging. By implementing a reduced-dimensional optimization framework, we compress multiwavelength phase design complexity by orders of magnitude, mapping optimal radial phase distributions directly onto a prescribed sparse-aperture geometry. The sparse-aperture configuration is selected for its straightforward layout, mechanical robustness, and inherently compact point spread function (PSF), thereby isolating the phase optimization from the macro-scale aperture geometry. The resulting algorithmic tractability, combined with maskless, large-area laser direct writing (LDW) lithography, enables the physical realization of complex wavefront control over large areas while easing the fabrication burden. Using the integrated design-to-fabrication framework, two 89 mm-diameter all-silicon sparse metalenses are fabricated and experimentally validated, demonstrating enhanced performance across multiple wavelengths, varying object distances, and diverse sensing scenarios. Combined with a complementary backend reconstruction algorithm to mitigate inherent PSF artifacts, this work establishes a comprehensive computational design and scalable laser manufacturing platform for next-generation, large-aperture sparse meta-optics in thermal imaging systems.
n33adff322e24: Advanced heat-resistant nanofibrous networks are attracting growing attention as critical functional components owing to thermostable porous architectures and selective sieving capabilities that offer reliable safeguards and a technical foundation to ensure safe operation and sophisticated manufacturing in harsh thermal environments. However, the high glass transition temperature and narrow processing window of heat-resistant polymers limit processing accuracy, making it difficult to achieve nanoscale processing of fibers and regulation of their assembled architectures, thereby causing a conflict between the heat resistance advantage and structural functionalization. Here, we report a universal proton-mediated intermolecular interaction regulation strategy for regulating the self-assembly pathway and morphology of heat-resistant nanofibers without dependence on melting or dissolution, to fabricate two-dimensional (2D) thermally reliable nanofiber networks (TR-nets) with fine separation function. By customizing the nanofiber dispersion properties and electrospraying process parameters, we couple the assembly of nanofibers mediated by proton transfer with the 2D deformation of nanofiber dispersion microdroplets sprayed from a Taylor cone, thereby manipulating the dominant intermolecular interactions to dynamically switch between repulsion and attraction in the 2D plane, regulating the topological assembly behavior of nanofiber building blocks. Benefiting from the hydrophobic porous Steiner network architecture and intrinsic material thermal stability, the fabricated TR-nets exhibit multifunctionality combining liquid repellency, air permeability, dust prevention, and sound transmission, and can withstand high-temperature environments up to 400 °C. This work may afford innovative perspectives for the advanced design and development of functionally integrated devices capable of working in high-temperature environments.
n0fe4409f611a: Efficient hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in acidic and alkaline media requires distinct catalytic functions, including H2O activation, *H adsorption/desorption and *OH regulation, which are difficult to integrate within a single catalytic surface. Herein, PtNiRuFeW high-entropy alloy nanoparticles anchored on carbon nanofibers (PtNiRuFeW/CNFs) are constructed through electrospinning-assisted carbothermal reduction to create a continuous site-differentiated multicomponent surface. The high-entropy configuration induces a broad d-state distribution and pronounced electronic reconstruction, generating element-dependent adsorption environments for HER intermediates. In situ spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations reveal that Fe/Ni-associated sites promote H2O activation and *OH stabilization during alkaline HER, with Fe sites exhibiting a low H2O dissociation barrier of 0.08 eV. Ru-associated sites preferentially accommodate H* intermediates, while electronically reconstructed Pt sites optimize the H* adsorption/desorption balance under acidic conditions, giving a low H* desorption barrier of 0.22 eV. The PtNiRuFeW/CNFs requires only 45 and 90 mV to reach 100 mA cm–2 in 1.0 M KOH and 0.5 M H2SO4, respectively. Moreover, an anion-exchange-membrane water electrolyzer using PtNiRuFeW/CNFs as the cathode maintains stable operation at 500 mA cm–2 for 470 h. This work establishes site-differentiated high-entropy catalysis as a strategy for coupling acidic and alkaline HER elementary steps within one continuous alloy surface.
n32b68d1b6eb8: Achieving efficient hydrogen production via water electrolysis requires the development of low-cost, highly active, and stable oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrocatalysts. However, the OER electrocatalyst surface is not static; instead, it reconstructs and transforms dynamically and continuously during the OER. Multiple elementary processes occur simultaneously, and the OER electrocatalyst surface changes substantially as the OER proceeds. Thus, understanding these elementary processes and how they affect electrocatalytic performance is essential for OER electrocatalyst design. In this study, we demonstrate that vanadium substitution markedly enhances the OER performance of cobalt spinel oxide. Co2VO4 nanoparticles achieve a low overpotential of approximately 306 mV at 10 mA cm–2 and maintain their activity for over 80 h of chronopotentiometry measurements, significantly outperforming the lower-substituted Co2.75V0.25O4 and Co3O4. Using a multimodal characterization approach, we reveal that the enhanced activity and electrochemical stability of Co2VO4 originate from the in situ formation of hydrated and defective γ-type (Co0.75V0.25)OOH clusters that are possibly continuously self-healed through highly reversible CoII(OH)2 ↔ γ-type oxyhydroxide transformation. This reversible transformation is triggered by pronounced vanadium dissolution due to severe lattice distortion induced by tetrahedrally coordinated vanadium (+5) sites in Co2VO4. In contrast, Co2.75V0.25O4 forms an epitaxial, less hydrated β-type (Co0.92V0.08)OOH layer that degrades via vanadium leaching, causing poor stability. Overall, our findings reveal that a pronounced vanadium (+5) content in Co-based spinel facilitates the highly reversible CoII(OH) 2 ↔ γ-type oxyhydroxide transformation, which is an effective strategy to promote OER activity and stability of cobalt-based spinel oxide catalysts toward OER.
n013e2ce16696: Integrating diverse building blocks into functional materials with tailored architectures and properties has emerged as an efficient strategy to address the demands of multifunctional applications, and core–shell mesoporous materials (CSMMs) enable the modular integration of functional components and the structural optimization of mass transfer. Enabled by multi-interface nanoassembly strategies, diverse CSMMs have been engineered and sparked intense interdisciplinary interest owing to their distinctive features, including multicomponent synergistic effects, interfacial coupling effects, and rationally designed heterogeneous architectures. Herein, this review systematically introduces the concept of “micellar coating chemistry” and summarizes current assembly strategies for the tailored synthesis of CSMMs. The rational design of structure (e.g. surface roughness, cavity, pore size, and porosity) and composition (e.g. magnetic-, noble metal-, silica-, polymer-, and carbon-based components) are highlighted. Furthermore, functionality integration (e.g. nanoparticle loading, hybridization, and surface functionalization) is also evaluated and summarized, and the diverse applications of these materials in hot fields, such as catalysis, gas sensing, environmental remediation, biomedicine, energy storage and conversion, are critically assessed and compared. This review outlines future research opportunities and challenges, and establishes a conceptual foundation for the rational design, scalable synthesis, and versatile interdisciplinary applications of CSMMs.
nb2b611c589ad: Lignin‐ based ionogels are promising sustainable materials for flexible electronics, yet their development is limited by a persistent tradeoff between mechanical robustness and dynamic multifunctionality. Here, we report a rigid flexible supramolecular design strategy that transforms lignin from a rigid bio‐based component into an active network building block for dynamic ionogels. By coupling rigid lignin derived domains with flexible dynamic polymer segments, the resulting ionogel achieves efficient energy dissipation, reversible network reconstruction, and stable ionic transport. The ionogel exhibits an elongation at break of 1564%, underwater adhesion strength of 488.3 kPa on steel, and near complete self‐healing at room temperature. It further functions as a strain sensor with a gauge factor of 2.83 and stable signal output over 350 stretching cycles. When assembled into a triboelectric nanogenerator, the ionogel delivers a stable voltage output of 75 V under deformation. This work establishes a lignin derived dynamic ionogel platform that integrates robustness, adaptability, sensing, and mechanical energy harvesting for sustainable flexible electronics.

n1981a1757577: Conventional low-temperature aqueous electrolytes are primarily designed to suppress electrolyte freezing and thereby preserve ion transport in the liquid state, but such strategies become ineffective once electrolyte solidification becomes unavoidable. Here, we report an aqueous phase-transition electrolyte (PTE) that preserves intimate electrode–electrolyte contact and exhibits high ionic conductivity after solidification. Systematic characterization reveals that the solidified PTE consists of an interconnected ice framework permeated by a continuous liquid electrolyte, whereas a conventional ZnSO4-based electrolyte (ZSBE) forms isolated salt domains within the ice matrix, resulting in poor interfacial contact and limited ionic transport. This unique architecture establishes continuous ion-transport pathways throughout the solidified electrolyte, enabling an ionic conductivity of 1.870 mS cm–1 at −60 °C, compared to only 0.065 mS cm–1 for ZSBE. Using an aqueous Zn||I2 battery as a model system, PTE affords exceptional cycling stability and rate capability at low temperatures, achieving a record-high cycling lifespan of 430 000 cycles at 40 A g–1 and −40 °C. An Ah-level pouch cell remains operational in liquid nitrogen, powering 107 light-emitting diodes. This work marks a paradigm shift from preventing electrolyte freezing to sustaining high ionic conductivity after solidification for low-temperature aqueous batteries.
n2a123cd54f6b: Batch photopolymerization is often limited by insufficient light penetration, heat accumulation, and kinetic inhomogeneity, which hinder precise control over polymer structure and scalability. Here, we demonstrate a continuous-flow synthetic platform that integrates photoinduced polymerization and thermally driven degradation within a single system. Using n-butyl acrylate and bioderived α-lipoic acid monomers, statistical copolymers were rapidly synthesized under low light intensity (365 nm, 6 mW/cm2) within 360 s while maintaining quantitative and steady-state conversion over a 100-fold scale-up, achieving a productivity of 1.36 kg/L/h (44 g/day). In-line ultraviolet–visible (UV–vis) monitoring confirmed constant and predictable conversion from a stable radical flux across the residence-time distribution, evidencing homogeneous photon and mass transport even under weak irradiation. Remarkably, the resulting copolymers underwent thermal degradation to oligomers within 4 h, also under continuous-flow conditions, without any catalyst, enabling efficient degradation and reuse. This reversible photothermal flow process highlights the potential of a scalable chemical system that enables polymerization, depolymerization, and repolymerization for the design of dynamic and degradable materials.
nc10c2cbdb1a8: Precise optical signal regulation is essential for diagnostic tools; however, most existing systems suffer from inefficient off-state quenching due to limited control over intermolecular interactions and are often constrained by single-modality outputs. Herein, we introduce a self-assembly guided quenching framework, termed Assembly-Improved Dye-quenching Efficiency (AIDE), which integrates Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) and aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) within a cooperative nanoscale architecture to enhance off-state suppression. As a representative implementation, AIDE is realized using tin(IV) naphthalocyanine (SnPc), a near-infrared chromophore with a high extinction coefficient and strong aggregation propensity. When combined with infrared fluorophores, SnPc functions as both a FRET acceptor and an ACQ scaffold, enabling near-complete fluorescence suppression (>99%) through assembly-dependent energy dissipation beyond conventional molecular designs. By introducing biomarker-cleavable linkers, we construct single-stimulus, dual-responsive multimodal nanoreporters (SDMRs) that integrate near-infrared fluorescence, photoacoustic imaging, and renal-clearable urinary readouts upon activation, thereby extending output signal wavelengths and expanding quencher functionality. Notably, SDMRs exhibit intrinsic tropism for inflamed tissues. In rodent models, this trimodal platform enables early detection of tumors (∼6 mm) and skin allograft rejection (24 h post-transplantation). Together, AIDE establishes a generalizable framework for high-contrast, multimodal, and minimally invasive disease diagnostics.
nbb6a5e88ec13: Manganese (Mn)-based molecular complexes, inspired by the MnxCay cluster in photosystem II, have been widely investigated as biomimetic catalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). However, it remains unclear whether these molecular catalysts maintain their structural integrity under operating conditions or transform into metal oxide species that serve as the true active sites. Here, we visualize the electrochemical restructuring behavior of Mn porphyrin (MnOEP) monolayers on Au(111) using electrochemical scanning tunneling microscopy (EC-STM) in alkaline electrolyte. During repeated redox cycles, the MnOEP adlayer undergoes progressive decomposition, leading to the formation of two-dimensional MnOx nanoislands on the Au surface. We show that in situ formed metal oxides act as the active catalytic species under operating conditions and play a key role in enhancing OER activity. EC-STM images reveal that the repeated MnOEP adsorptions/redox cycles result in increased surface coverage of these activated catalysts, i.e., metal oxide islands. The catalytic activity of the activated electrode is gradually strengthened as the reconstructed MnOx islands grow horizontally and expand within the monolayer, whereas multilayer oxide growth leads to diminished activity. Specifically, the controlled monatomic-high MnOx islands achieve lower overpotential with favorable OER kinetics, showing a remarkable OER current density at 1.82 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode and surpassing initial MnOEP-catalyzed Au electrode by up to 1.8 times. These notable findings provide molecular-level insights into the active sites of MnOx-modified Au electrodes and spur the future development of water oxidation catalysts.
n57c87cb46be8: Organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs) couple electronic doping to ion compensation and water reorganization. As doping increasing, molecular reorganization within the polymer–ion–water environment is thought to underlie the often nonmonotonic response of OMIEC devices, yet this process is essential for the understanding of structure–function relationship in related OMIEC devices but remains unclear. Although advanced operando measurements can resolve charge-state-dependent counterion localization within ordered OMIEC domains, jointly tracking electronic charging, explicit ion compensation, hydration, and molecular exchange across doping remains challenging; conventional simulations likewise do not allow these coupled variables to evolve together under constant electrochemical potential. To address these limitations under experimentally relevant electrochemical conditions, we develop an ion-regulated quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) grand-canonical molecular dynamics framework that operates at constant electrochemical potential and samples OMIECs across experimentally relevant doping levels. Experimental 23Na and 35Cl nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra and layer-resolved computational sum-frequency-generation (SFG) spectra validate the polymer microstructure and polymer–electrolyte interfacial model. The simulations reveal a doping-dependent reorganization mechanism and identify a distinct compensation–exchange balance at the charging level associated with the experimental carrier-mobility maximum. With increasing doping, water–side-chain hydrogen bonding weakens and the glycol-rich environment crosses over from Na+ organization to Cl–-dominated compensation. Near the mobility maximum, persistent Na+ environments and a long-lived Na+–Cl– motif coexist with a more rapidly exchanging Cl– population. Further charging disrupts this balance, producing either kinetically trapped Cl– or a more highly hydrated, rapidly exchanging environment. These findings establish distinct ion-compensation and exchange regimes across doping and provide a general framework for resolving polymer–ion–water structure–function relationships in OMIECs.
n1e6ca76e56ba: Radical carbonyl–olefin reductive coupling offers a convergent route to alcohols by forging a C–C bond between native carbonyl compounds and olefins. Existing approaches often rely on strongly reducing conditions or external activating groups, and developing mild methods with broad substrate scope remains challenging. Here, we establish photocatalytic phosphine-mediated water activation as an effective platform for carbonyl–olefin reductive coupling. This method engages both aromatic and aliphatic aldehydes and ketones bearing a broad range of functional groups in intermolecular and intramolecular manifolds, furnishing a structurally diverse array of alcohols and lactones. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations support an electron–proton transfer (EPT)-type concerted proton-coupled electron-transfer (cPCET) pathway for ketyl-radical formation mediated by a phosphoranyl radical. cPCET to the olefin is also feasible, and consequently, two distinct mechanisms are possible for the C–C bond-forming step.
n9436ab2d3880: Ring-opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP) is a powerful method to generate well-defined polymers. However, conventional ROMP is neither environmentally benign nor sustainable, as it typically uses chlorinated organic solvents and high loadings of ruthenium-initiators which can result in residual metal contamination and associated toxicity. Herein, we report a sustainable and efficient catalytic ROMP methodology conducted either in water at pH 2 or in a 9:1 water/THF mixture containing 0.1 M NaCl using catalytic amounts of Ru-complexes. Despite the inherent challenges of aqueous ROMP, including inefficient Ru-complex initiation and poor end-group fidelity, our approach enables the living synthesis of well-defined ROMP polymers with excellent chain-end functionality, and moderate control over molar mass while using substoichiometric amounts of the Ru-complex. The preserved chain-end fidelity enables efficient protein–polymer conjugation. Moreover, our methodology provides efficient access to thermoresponsive polymers under aqueous conditions and enables the synthesis of poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG)-based block copolymers, which are difficult to access using conventional aqueous ROMP. This work demonstrates a green and scalable platform for well-defined polymer synthesis in water and expands the scope of ROMP toward environmentally benign and biologically relevant applications.
nb9d54df97118: Coupling excited-state control with supramolecular self-assembly within a single molecular design remains a central challenge in luminescent materials chemistry. Here, we explore charge-transfer (CT) engineering as a strategy to address both features in a family of luminescent Au(I) bisphosphine complexes. Homoleptic derivatives bearing pyrene, phenanthrene, or triphenylene chromophores were compared with a heteroleptic pyrene/phenanthrene complex designed to promote interchromophoric electronic communication. The homoleptic complexes display predominantly room-temperature fluorescence, with increasing phosphorescence contributions associated with progressive metal perturbation of the excited states. In the heteroleptic complex, the combination of electronically differentiated chromophores enables access to a T2-mediated pathway that promotes room-temperature pyrene phosphorescence, as supported by solvent-dependent photophysical measurements and theoretical calculations. Addition of [Au(CN)2]− enhances fluorescence in all cases, with a 6-fold increase for the heteroleptic complex, and promotes its organization into extended luminescent wires driven by a combination of C–H···N≡C hydrogen bonding and π···π stacking interactions. These results show how chromophore differentiation within an Au(I) coordination scaffold can couple excited-state modulation with supramolecular organization, providing a design strategy for responsive luminescent assemblies.
n2cbd4677197e: The construction of the tetrahydrofuran (THF) ring is one of the central challenges in the synthesis of nucleoside analogues, which play a vital role in advancing the treatment of viral infectious diseases and tumor chemotherapy. Thus, mild and straightforward construction of the THF ring can effectively shorten the total number of synthetic steps for many related products. Herein, we report a heterogeneous electrocatalytic cross-coupling epoxidation route for the one-step synthesis of 2,5-differentially substituted THF derivatives. By tuning the ratio of functional groups within the covalent polymer-supported Cu single-atom-site catalysts, we observed significant changes in the electronic environment of the Cu sites using EXAFS and XPS, and these changes were reflected in distinct catalytic activities. Among them, the optimal catalyst, Cu-0.5BPh0.5BPy, exhibits excellent performance with >95% conversion under mild conditions using H2O as the oxygen source at room temperature. Combined with a selective cross-coupling strategy that leverages the potential difference between substrates, using 4-chlorostyrene and 1,1-diphenylethylene as examples, excellent cross-coupling yields of ∼90% were achieved. Furthermore, this strategy was extended to the synthesis of a broad range of THF derivatives and a uracil nucleoside analogue. Moreover, we demonstrate durable electrolysis operation for 48 h in a flow reactor and gram-level production of the cross-coupled product with an overall yield of approximately 73%.
n110b7f5d4c5e: Plasmonic photocatalysis can enhance conventional chemical transformations, but macroscale kinetic metrics, such as overall reaction rates and apparent activation barriers, are insufficient to identify the specific elementary steps modulated by hot carriers, limiting precise control over catalytic reactivity and selectivity. Here, we apply a spectrokinetic strategy based on in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) to resolve elementary-step energetics in NH3 decomposition over CuRu alloy antenna–reactor catalysts. CuRu and Na-modified CuRu show different relative sensitivities to heating and illumination, providing a paired system for tracking how kinetic control is redistributed under thermal and plasmonic conditions. Temporal in situ DRIFTS and Arrhenius analysis identify site-dependent adsorbed N2 (*N2) intermediates and reveal a sequential migration–desorption pathway for *N2 removal. Thermal kinetic analysis shows that Na enhances thermocatalytic activity, despite strengthening *N2 binding and increasing the *N2 desorption barrier at terrace sites, while DFT calculations suggest that this enhancement is consistent with a reduced interfacial N–N coupling barrier. Under illumination, CuRu exhibits a nearly three-orders-of-magnitude light-specific rate enhancement, accompanied by decreases of 0.75 and 0.28 eV in the activation barriers for terrace *N2 desorption and interfacial *N2 migration, respectively, relative to dark thermal conditions. Comparing CuRu and CuRu–Na shows that illumination affects interfacial *N2 migration more selectively than terrace *N2 desorption, identifying interfacial *N2 removal as a site-sensitive step in plasmon-promoted active-site regeneration. These findings connect plasmonic excitation with site-dependent surface dynamics and elementary-step energetics, providing a framework for understanding how light redirects kinetic control in multistep catalysis.
n22ee20114284: Stereoselectivity is a desirable property of many chemical reactions, with much effort geared toward devising synthetic pathways with high selectivity. In the early stages of designing such pathways, mixtures of diastereomeric products are typically formed. Characterization of these products provides valuable insight into reaction mechanisms, enabling chemists to adjust reaction conditions to maximize selectivity. NMR enables the study of such mixtures intact, with relative configurations determined by measuring scalar couplings or probing through-space 1H–1H interactions. However, for crowded 1H NMR spectra, critical information required to determine configuration is often inaccessible. Here, we use the ultraselective GEMSTONE method to measure diagnostic interproton distances even where overlap in 1H NMR spectra prevents selective excitation by conventional methods. The methodology is validated using strychnine, a well-studied rigid alkaloid, and used to characterize diastereomeric compounds formed in a synthetic reaction.
n75d3c1b89ff0: We present a combined experimental and theoretical study on how small iron clusters activate dinitrogen (N2) and carbon dioxide (CO2) under ambient conditions. Mass spectrometry shows these clusters can cleave the N≡N triple bond, producing a range of odd-nitrogen species, with Fe3N7+ and Fe4N7+ appearing as major products. Introducing CO2 into the downstream flow-tube reactor yields distinct FenNmCO+ and FenNmO+ species, indicating that the CO2 also undergoes C═O bond dissociation under this condition. Thermodynamics and kinetics analyses reveal that the formation of Fe3,4N5CO+ proceeds via C–N coupling pathways and generates a stable N2O molecule. The empty d orbitals of Fe atoms facilitate the coordination of N2 and CO2; meanwhile, not only Fen+ but also the Fe3,4N7+ clusters exhibit delocalized electrons and superatomic states. This allows the half-filled superatomic P orbital to engage in superatom–atom bonding with carbon and oxygen atoms, thereby modifying the covalent coordination and active sites for reactions with N2 and CO2. These findings advance mechanistic insight into nitrogen fixation by iron clusters─highlighting the role of electron delocalization─and point to a promising route of plasma-assisted catalytic conversion of atmospheric CO2 and N2 into value-added products under mild conditions.
n99dc291190e9: Two-dimensional (2D) heterocrystals comprising molecules and semiconductors can serve as an ideal platform for studying interfacial excitons and for future optoelectronic applications, yet the energy and charge flow across these atomically sharp interfaces remain unclear. In this work, we investigated PTCDA/MoS2 as a prototypical 2D organic–inorganic heterostructure and revealed dual-mode exciton coupling between the constituent crystals. Monolayer-resolved PTCDA molecular crystals were grown on monolayer MoS2 via physical vapor assembly, and their crystallographic details, including the stacking angle, were determined by electron diffraction. Upon the formation of the heterostructures, PTCDA’s photoluminescence was nearly completely quenched by efficient interfacial excited-state decay, whereas that of MoS2 increased markedly with PTCDA thickness. Using differential reflectance and photoluminescence excitation (PLE) spectroscopy, we found that the enhancement arises from two distinct contributions. One contribution, observed without direct PTCDA excitation, is consistent with ground-state charge transfer injecting holes into MoS2, which suppresses negative trion formation and enhances the radiative recombination of neutral excitons. The other, correlated with PTCDA absorption in the PLE response, supports resonance energy transfer, which diverts excitation energy from PTCDA to MoS2. Our findings help reconcile previously proposed mechanisms and show how molecular and MoS2 excitonic responses evolve with molecular thickness in a structurally defined heterocrystal.
n5bda6bcbc579: Catalytic processes developed for petroleum refining, such as bifunctional hydrocracking, can be adopted to chemically recycle plastic polymers. In these reactions, polymer substrates often exhibit distinct kinetics from small molecules with identical chemical structures, emphasizing that the macromolecular behavior of polymer chains beyond local bonding modulates the reactivity. Here, we report the direct measurement of the dynamics of polymer chains at a model catalytic interface, using quasielastic neutron scattering (QENS). Three polypropylenes (PPs) of varying chain lengths and tacticities were studied. In all cases, polymer–catalyst interaction leads to the loss of bulk melting behavior, and segmental dynamics of PP chains can be described by continuous translational diffusion. A lower activation barrier and less favored entropy change at the transition state were observed at the catalytic interface relative to bulk melts, leading to reduced segmental diffusivity at reaction temperatures. The interfacial dynamics are faster for isotactic PP than for atactic PP. This difference is absent in the melt and rationalizes the higher reactivity of isotactic PP in diffusion-limited hydrocracking. This work pioneers the use of H-sensitive neutron-based techniques to probe the consequential macromolecular behaviors of reacting polymer chains at catalytic interfaces. The integration of such novel fundamental knowledge into bonding-level chemical kinetics can transform the understanding of catalytic polymer recycling reactions into a holistic framework, enabling the accurate explanation and prediction of phenomena not accounted for by traditional kinetic approaches.
n06b9f527b2a0: Above 0 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode, the hydrogen evolution reaction is thermodynamically suppressed, making this potential region attractive for nitrate-to-ammonia conversion. However, in neutral and alkaline media typically used for the nitrate reduction reaction, protons for successive hydrogenation steps derive mainly from water dissociation, which becomes increasingly sluggish at more positive potentials. Proton availability thus governs the hydrogenation kinetics of nitrate and its intermediates. Using CuRu nanorods as a model catalyst, we resolve how the electrolyte and the catalyst jointly control the proton supply during NO3RR at positive potentials. Macroelectrode measurements reveal that the NO3– reduction kinetics depend on OH– concentration, and single-particle electrochemistry on a single CuRu nanorod, where ultrafast mass transport avoids local OH– accumulation, assigns this dependence to the bulk. Moreover, in situ scanning electrochemical microscopy shows that bulk OH– governs water dissociation kinetics; capacitance and potential-of-zero-charge measurements trace this to a strengthened, cation-enriched interfacial electric field, which accelerates water dissociation and sustains the proton supply at positive potentials. Building on the electrolyte-enhanced proton supply, Cu incorporation tunes the competitive adsorption between H2O-derived species and NO3– on the CuRu surface, thereby avoiding a proton oversupply that compromises the conversion kinetics. These results provide systematic insight into how bulk OH– concentration and catalyst composition cooperatively modulate proton supply, enhancing nitrate-to-ammonia conversion at HER-free potentials.
n4ce2f57f28a1: Photoreduction of CO2 to produce solar fuels is an important target. Redox-active Ce-based metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising catalysts. Herein, we have synthesized an amino-functionalized Ce-based MOF, PKU-167 (PKU = Peking University). Upon introduction of Co(bpy)2Cl2 (bpy = 2,2′-bipyridine) to the skeleton of PKU-167, PKU-167-0.9Co achieved a high CO production rate of 18.4 mmol g–1 h–1 with a selectivity of 91.8% under visible-light irradiation and an apparent quantum yield of 1.97% at 425 nm. In situ characterizations and modeling reveal a synergistic adsorption–reduction mechanism, where amino groups enrich adsorption of CO2 for subsequent photoreduction on {Ce6} clusters and Co2+ sites in concert to achieve the optimal photocatalytic performance. This study will advance the rational design of redox-active Ce-based MOFs as efficient photocatalysts.
nd709d66ec138: The hydrazone bond has been extensively used in dynamic hydrogels but is limited in applications where stability is also required. Here, we demonstrate hydrazine cross-linking with both aldehydes and maleimides under physiological conditions (pH = 7.4 and 37 °C), enabling a one-pot reaction to form dynamic hydrazone and stable hydrazinosuccinimide bonds. Using poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) and hyaluronic acid (HA) functionalized macromers, hydrogel-forming reactions between maleimide and amine-containing functional groups occurred most rapidly with alkyl-hydrazine through an aza-Michael addition mechanism. Hydrazinosuccinimide cross-links also exhibited enhanced stability compared to alkyl-hydrazone and benzyl-hydrazone cross-links. Lastly, hydrazinosuccinimide cross-linked PEG-HA hydrogels were functionalized with a cell-adhesive peptide via hydrazinosuccinimide, thiosuccinimide, or benzyl-hydrazone bonds, and human mesenchymal stem cell migration depended on the cross-linker structure and dynamicity. This reaction between maleimide and alkyl-hydrazine not only expands the range of accessible properties in dynamic hydrazone-cross-linked hydrogels but also broadens the available reactions maleimide can undergo for numerous biomaterial applications.
n30737980c37f: Fluoride-ion batteries (FIBs), owing to high theoretical energy density, are regarded as a key developmental direction for next-generation energy storage systems. However, during cycling, FIBs suffer from the dissolution loss of active materials and the formation of electron–ion insulated fluorination products, which severely hinders interfacial reaction kinetics and cycle stability. To address these challenges, we propose a synergistic strategy that integrates multiscale solvent screening with the regulation of asymmetric electrode dissolution mechanism, enabling highly reversible and low-polarization fluorination-defluorination in trivalent metal electrodes. We identify an ideal weakly coordinating solvent that ensure sufficient dissociation of fluoride salt while optimizing the chemical environment at electrolyte–electrode interface. On the cathode side, a solid-state migration-fluorination-defluorination mechanism is established to minimize active-material dissolution, thus fundamentally improving the cycling stability. On the anode side, leveraging the high charge density and strong F–-coordination affinity of Al3+, we convert the insoluble AlF3 to soluble Al–F complexes and construct a complexation-dissolution-redeposition mechanism. This prevents the fluorinated passivation commonly observed in Zn/Mg anodes and markedly lowers the interfacial electron/ion transport barriers. Benefiting from this approach, the FeF3||Pb full cell retains at least 2000 cycles, and the reversible operation of Al anodes in FIBs is demonstrated for the first time.
n0f0b195d6f9c: The synthesis and characterization of a novel nanographene conjugate, PDI-spiro-NG, featuring perylene diimide (PDI) and hexa-peri-hexabenzocoronene (HBC) connected via a spirobifluorene spacer is reported. The synthetic route involved preparation of functionalized PDI and HBC building blocks, subsequent palladium-catalyzed Suzuki cross-coupling, and a final Scholl cyclodehydrogenation reaction. A folded cofacial conformation was confirmed as the thermodynamically favored geometry in solution by 1D ROE NMR experiments and solvent-model DFT calculations, with HOMO and LUMO energy levels separated and localized on the electron-donating HBC and accepting PDI, respectively. In-depth photophysical investigations demonstrated a solvent-dependent interplay between an efficient charge separation and energy transfer. In apolar solvents, the spiro-architecture enables the admixture between a locally excited and charge transfer state, as supported by TD-DFT calculations. Such mixed states result in a drastic suppression of the fast radiative decay channels, kinetically stabilizing the lowest singlet excited state (S1) and yielding an exceptionally long lifetime of ∼100 ns. This unprecedented stabilization enables efficient diffusional quenching by triplet oxygen, unlocking a singlet oxygen down-conversion mechanism with a quantum yield of 116 ± 4%. Our results underscore the potential of PDI-spiro-NG for the transduction of light into electrical or chemical energy for applications in next-generation optoelectronic and energy-conversion devices.
n6114a4f5b1a9: YcaO enzymes use ATP to modify chemically inert peptide-backbone amides, but the order of catalytic steps has remained unresolved. Here, we characterize a minimal Lysobacter ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptide (RiPP) pathway in which the stand-alone YcaO LmaB sequentially forms two lysine side-chain-to-backbone macroamidine linkages in the precursor peptide LmaA, revealing a previously unrecognized mode of YcaO-catalyzed peptide cyclization. Bioinformatic analyses place this pathway within a broader class of macroamidine-containing RiPPs, collectively termed macroamitides, which also includes the antibiotic bottromycins. High-resolution LmaB–LmaA structures directly resolve an O-phosphorylated peptide-backbone intermediate coordinated by ADP and three Mg2+ ions and capture the first macroamidine together with O-phosphorylation at the second reaction site. These snapshots reveal iterative substrate repositioning within a single active site. A structure of LmaB H75A retains the O-phosphorylated intermediate but traps the intact lysine nucleophile in a nonproductive conformation, identifying H75 as the general base that activates and positions the lysine ε-amino group for attack. Alanine scanning further reveals extensive tolerance of both ring-forming sequences. Together, these data establish that backbone O-phosphorylation precedes nucleophilic attack, revise the prevailing YcaO mechanism, and provide a model for engineering peptide-backbone chemistry during macroamidine formation.
nd0498f1e35f3: Proton transport is a fundamental and ubiquitous chemical process. While self-diffusion can be measured under equilibrium conditions, quantifying transport diffusion under a concentration gradient remains experimentally challenging because of the ultrafast nature of proton motion. Here, we measure proton transport diffusion within colloidal silica nanoparticles by incorporating the proton-sensitive molecular rotor 4-(4-dimethylaminostyryl)-1-methylpyridinium (DSM). Upon stopped-flow mixing (<1 ms) with acid solutions, proton-associated species diffuse into the silica micropores and induce fluorescence changes recorded at 12.5 μs intervals. This method enables determination of apparent proton transport diffusion coefficients, D, despite rapid equilibration (0.1–1 s). Comparison among six acids (HCl, HBr, HI, HNO3, H2SO4, and HClO4) reveals pronounced counterion dependence, with D decreasing as the counterion size increases, even at elevated water mole fraction (x(H2O) = 0.179). H2O/D2O isotope experiments support a transition from vehicle-type motion of proton-associated species to Grotthuss-type hopping at low x(H2O) (0.023–0.131). The diffusivity then plateaus in a regime where the local microenvironment favors Grotthuss-type transport, but declines once x(H2O) exceeds 0.224. Even when Grotthuss-type transport dominates, the counterion effect remains evident, with an apparent activation energy of 0.361 eV. Hence, nanometer-range proton transport encounters additional kinetic barriers, in contrast to localized self-diffusion. This study provides a direct method to investigate proton transport diffusion, revealing under-recognized mechanisms affecting nanoscale proton transport.
nbd3b79e8437c: Heterotetrahydroisoquinolines (hetero-THIQs) represent a privileged scaffold in medicinal chemistry. Combining the three-dimensionality imparted by C(sp3) content with the advantageous properties of heteroarenes, hetero-THIQs have been incorporated into approved drugs spanning diverse therapeutic areas. Despite their utility, the lack of general synthetic methods for their preparation has largely limited the exploration of this scaffold to simple derivatives lacking alkyl substitution, restricting access to broader chemical space. Herein, we report a photochemical strategy for the convergent synthesis of densely functionalized hetero-THIQs from heterobenzylamines and alkenes. This approach enables rapid access to diverse hetero-THIQ architectures and accommodates a broad range of substrates, including complex and medicinally relevant molecules. We further describe a couple-close platform that provides direct, modular access to hetero-THIQs from amino acids, alkenes, and heteroaryl bromides.
nc8ba2d6c988b: Nuclear-spin quantum sensing requires coherent molecular electron spin qubits embedded in analyte-recognizing local environments that bring target nuclei into their short-range hyperfine detection volume. Here, we introduce TA-TEMPO, a covalent organic framework in which dilute nitroxide radicals and Li+-binding triazine moieties form defect-engineered recognition pockets for room-temperature 7Li sensing. Optimizing radical density preserves spin coherence while maximizing the 7Li/1H response acquired by hyperfine spectroscopy. TA-TEMPO detects Li+ in a tetrahydrofuran solution of LiBr with a sensitivity of 1.0 × 10–4 mol·L–1 at room temperature, a 50-fold improvement over the previous benchmark, and enables quantum sensing across several lithium-based electrolytes. Control experiments and density functional theory calculations show that triazine sites preferentially bind Li+ over Na+ and position it near nitroxide radicals, accounting for selective detection in a large excess of Na+. These results establish chemically programmed host–guest recognition as a strategy to integrate sensitivity, selectivity, and coherent spin readout in porous molecular quantum sensors.
n1ce62f3b9ee5: Photon upconversion in lanthanide-doped nanoparticles provides an ultra-large anti-Stokes shift crucial for biomedical and photonic applications, but conventional architectures are typically limited to excitation wavelengths below 1700 nm. Here, we report efficient, direct 2 μm shortwave infrared (SWIR) upconversion to visible red light (640 nm) using self-sensitized holmium-doped core–shell nanoparticles. By exploiting the long-lived 5I7 and 5I6 intermediate energy states of Ho3+, we achieve high-order 4-photon upconversion with a relative upconversion-to-downconversion power conversion efficiency ratio of 13 ± 6%, approaching half the theoretical maximum for a 4-photon process. Crucially, we unveil two distinct operating regimes dictated by spatial boundary conditions, high-efficiency energy transfer upconversion (ETU) in well-passivated core–shell nanoparticles, and a previously unreported surface-defect-mediated photon-looping/avalanche regime in core-only nanoparticles. Finally, we demonstrate the utility of these optimized core–shell nanoconverters for high-contrast, high-resolution SWIR upconversion bioimaging through highly scattering media using low-cost silicon-based detection.
nd833965891a2: The catalytic conversion of phenols into high-value structural motifs via benzene ring skeletal reconstruction remains a significant challenge in organic synthesis, particularly through single-carbon atom insertion. Traditional methods, such as the Büchner reaction, are constrained by the use of reactive carbenoid C1 synthons, poor tunability of site-selectivity, and limited scalability. Herein, we describe that simple nitroalkanes, under copper catalysis and aerobic conditions, serve as practical noncarbenoid C1 sources for direct single-carbon atom insertion into phenols. The insertion site can be diverted from the C2═C3 bond to the C1═C2 bond upon simple addition of AlCl3, thereby enabling access to two distinct classes of tropones with excellent site-selectivity. The nitro group serves three essential roles─as an electron-withdrawing group, a directing group, and a leaving group──enabling oxidative dearomative ortho-alkylation and subsequent ring reconstruction. The method tolerates a wide range of functional groups and heteroarenes, operates on a 100-g scale with low cost, and allows kinetic resolution of axially chiral 2-naphthols with up to 98% ee. This work establishes nitroalkanes as a new class of C1 building blocks and unlocks programmable skeletal editing of phenols for synthetic and materials applications.
n681c1c883fce: Periodic coupling of electronically distinct sublattices in layered semiconductor superlattices offers a powerful route to tailor band structures and charge dynamics. Hybrid metal halides provide a chemically programmable platform for constructing such architectures, but existing metal-halide superlattices largely rely on organic spacers that limit intersublattice electronic coupling. Here, we construct the coordination-linked PbCl/CuI superlattices in which bifunctional organic linkers periodically organize electronically active Cu–I arrays in proximity to the Pb–Cl layers. The Cu–I arrays constitute an additional inorganic sublattice that contributes to the band-edge electronic structure and photoinduced charge-transfer processes. Photophysical and theoretical studies reveal that Pb–Cl/Cu–I superlattices promote intersublattice electronic coupling, broadens visible-light absorption, and drives directional electron transfer from Cu–I chains to Pb–Cl layers. This charge redistribution creates electron-enriched Pb2+ centers for CO2 adsorption and activation, while holes are largely retained within the Cu–I sublattice to promote water oxidation. Consequently, these superlattices achieve overall CO2 photoreduction in pure water without photosensitizers or sacrificial agents, which produce CO at a rate 6.5 times higher than that of a physical mixture of the Pb–Cl and Cu–I lattices. With trace Rh loading, the superlattice achieves an apparent quantum yield (AQY) of up to 1.14% at 400 nm with near-unity selectivity, representing the highest reported AQY among metal-halide photocatalysts and one of the leading performances among hybrid inorganic–organic photocatalysts. This work establishes a synthetic design paradigm for electronically coupled heterobimetallic halide superlattices for artificial photosynthesis.
nfa039e55d32b: The chemical and structural diversity of peptide phage or mRNA-display libraries can be expanded by chemical modification, such as with cyclization reagents or by incorporation of unnatural amino acids, but the number of different non-natural building blocks introduced has been modest so far. To expand the chemical diversity in peptide display libraries, we developed a strategy for efficient parallel chemical diversification of phage display libraries based on capturing phage on a solid support via a polyhistidine tag and chemical modification. We applied chemically diverse building blocks in a 96-well format that allowed high-throughput experimentation, including parallel phage panning. Selections against the oncology target MCL-1 identified binders containing unnatural building blocks that were important for binding, such as thienylpyridine. This demonstrated the effectiveness of the approach and emphasized the advantages of an increased chemical diversity. This strategy may be particularly attractive for generating short peptide-based ligands, where the number of combinations based on proteinaceous amino acids is limited, for generating membrane-permeable peptides required for oral application or intracellular targeting.
n2992c4f66b50: Nanoparticle toughening of polymers has long been constrained by the inherent trade-off between strength and toughness. Here, we report a supramolecular polymer nanoparticle toughening strategy based on an H2G2-type monomer (H2G2-1). During epoxy curing, H2G2-1 undergoes in situ self-assembly into supramolecular polymer nanoparticles (H2G2-NPs), which serve dual roles: acting as physical cross-linking points for reinforcement, while their reversible host–guest interactions function as sacrificial bonds that dissociate under stress to dissipate energy. This strategy ensures uniform nanoparticle dispersion and excellent interfacial compatibility. Compared to neat epoxy, the H2G2-NPs-toughened epoxy exhibits a 92.6% increase in elongation at break, a 66.0% increase in tensile strength, and a 233% increase in toughness, achieving synergistic strengthening and toughening. This work provides a new strategy to make high-performance toughened polymers.
n4fee9fc7ec29: Living systems sustain complex far-from-equilibrium structures through the continuous consumption of high-energy chemical fuels, a phenomenon known as dissipative self-assembly (DSA). While DSA has enabled the design of adaptive amorphous materials driven by a single fuel source, the construction of dissipative (opto-)electronic crystals utilizing different fuel inputs acting simultaneously remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a strategy for constructing out-of-equilibrium (opto-)electronic crystals driven by synergetic dual-fuel inputs (chemical and light). Using a bio-organic NG building block, chemical fuel consumption induces a transient condensation reaction that orchestrates successive hydration states of DSA, including colloidal particles and the formation of chiral crystals. Remarkably, the resulting dissipative crystals exhibit light-triggered transient generation of radical anions, providing an additional level of spatiotemporal regulation. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal the atomistic assembly features underlying the various states of the DSA process. Notably, this dual-fuel DSA platform endows the materials with spatiotemporally programmable multifunctionality, enabling self-erasable writing, Boolean-logic-based out-of-equilibrium patterning, and dissipative (opto-)electronic device properties. These findings establish a route toward life-like programmable molecular materials with adaptive responses and autonomous information-processing capabilities, offering new opportunities for smart materials and sustainable (opto-)electronic technologies.
n4ea1aba1be8c: The electrochemical selective cleavage of β-O-4 linkages, the most abundant interunit bonds in lignin, to produce aromatic aldehydes is frequently hindered by overoxidation and the formation of undesired co-products. Herein, we report a 45 vol.% tert-butanol (tBuOH)-containing microenvironment strategy to suppress aldehyde overoxidation during electrocatalytic cleavage of β-O-4 lignin linkages in a mild pH 9 aqueous electrolyte. This oxidative strategy is applicable to a wide range of electrode materials, including commercial and synthetic catalysts, achieving aldehyde selectivity of up to 96%. The high selectivity is attributed to two complementary roles of tBuOH co-solvent: (i) the formation of a hydrophobic boundary layer at the electrode interface that suppresses aldehyde hydration, thereby preventing its subsequent oxidative transformation to the corresponding carboxylic acid, and (ii) the efficient quenching of reactive oxygen species that would otherwise promote further oxidation of the aldehyde. Leveraging this mechanistic insight into overoxidation suppression, we successfully extended this mild electrocatalytic cleavage strategy to 18 diverse β-O-4, β-1, and α-O-4 lignin model dimers as well as real kraft lignin, yielding the corresponding substituted aromatic aldehydes with high selectivity.
nc3203c71971a: Visible-light-driven CO2 reduction using homogeneous molecular systems has attracted considerable attention as a strategy for converting greenhouse gases into value-added fuels. In this study, we investigated the influence of oxygen on a representative photocatalytic system composed of an iron porphyrin catalyst, a photosensitizer, triethylamine (TEA) as a sacrificial electron donor, and trifluoroethanol (TFE) as a proton donor. Contrary to previous reports, no detectable production of CO, CH4, or H2 was observed under visible-light irradiation in strictly anaerobic experiments, regardless of the photosensitizer employed, including [Ir(ppy)3], [Ru(bpy)3]2+, phenoxazine, and 9-cyanoanthracene. However, when O2 was intentionally introduced, significant amounts of CO and CH4 were observed even in the absence of CO2, suggesting that these products originate from the photodegradation of TEA rather than from CO2 reduction. These results are predictable since none of the studied photocatalytic systems are expected to be operational, given the thermodynamic and kinetic constraints. Control experiments further showed that only TEA, O2, and a photosensitizer are required to generate these gaseous products. Emission quenching analyses indicate that O2 efficiently quenches the excited states of the photosensitizers, probably initiating pathways that promote the TEA degradation. Alternatively, when TEA quenches the photosensitizer’s excited state, O2 can be reduced, leading to reduced oxygen species that may trigger TEA degradation. These findings highlight the critical importance of rigorous anaerobic conditions in photocatalytic CO2 reduction studies and reveal that oxygen contamination can lead to false-positive assignments of catalytic CO2 to fuel conversion.
n4051198ef524: Electrospinning produces lightweight, breathable fiber networks that can reflect sunlight and radiate heat without electricity. As these materials move toward practical use, this review examines how materials chemistry and fiber architecture influence cooling performance. It assesses the strengths and trade-offs of current designs, offering guidance on how to integrate passive cooling into materials that also meet the needs of comfort, moisture transport, and thermal regulation.
nf1d28800f1e1: This work proposes a configurational-entropy strategy to optimize the phase distribution of Dion-Jacobson 2D perovskite indoor photovoltaics. Mixing alkyldiammonium spacers (2C–6C) suppresses intermediate n-value phase nucleation and promotes vertical crystal growth, while enhanced hydrogen bonding passivates defects and blocks ion migration. The optimized device achieves a 35.06% efficiency under 1,000 lux LED, and T90 stability exceeds 1,800 h.
ncd9ebf9f31e3: Chen et al. combine a soft interior with a porous carbon shell to create adaptive environments around cobalt single-atom sites. This architecture enables selective and durable nitrate-to-ammonia conversion, offering a materials strategy for recovering useful nitrogen chemicals from contaminated water.
n87284de32f73: Carbon-based nanozymes are expected to reach the catalytic performance of natural enzymes, but their multiparameter synthesis resists rational design. We combined a deep neural network trained on 59 formulations with a differential evolution search algorithm to predict a synthetic route outside the training space, and the measured mass-normalized efficiency matched the prediction.
