The optimized VS-1 showed a particle size of 2.2 nm, with Fe atoms dispersed and coordinated to approximately 7–8 light atoms (N/O). The optimized VS-1 exhibits a Michaelis constant (Km) of 0.149 mM and a maximum reaction velocity of 2.67 × 10–6 M s–1, demonstrating a substrate affinity approximately three times higher than that of natural horseradish peroxidase. Furthermore, mechanistic investigations based primarily on electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, supported by radical-scavenger trends, identify the superoxide anion radical as the dominant reactive species for substrate oxidation. This work provides a highly active carbon-based catalytic carbon dot for sensing.
nb8cb7826bb18: State-of-charge (SOC) is a central parameter in battery management systems for electric vehicles, directly affecting driving range, power delivery, safety, and battery lifetime. However, real-time and high-precision SOC monitoring remains a challenge for practical batteries. Here, we report a capacity and electrochromism decoupling strategy for real-time SOC monitoring of high-areal-capacity electrochromic batteries. The bilayer cathode combines a pure electrochromic coloration layer with an underlying conductive, high-loading capacity layer, thereby spatially separating optical readout from high-capacity storage. The device delivers an areal capacity of 3.4 mAh cm–2 with 97.8% capacity retention after 300 cycles. The monotonic SOC–Hue relationship with 1% SOC intervals was established by converting in situ reflectance spectra into Hue values. The modulation of reflectance-peak wavelength shift retains 81.2% after 1000 coloration cycles. This architecture provides a route toward batteries with built-in optical state reporting for advanced battery management.
n1a2e830dcba4: The Casimir effect, where conducting plates restrict electromagnetic vacuum modes, is a cornerstone of quantum field theory but has no known analogue in semiconductor excitonic systems. Here we report a Casimir-like excitonic state in twin-structured type-II core/shell quantum dots, where the two-core geometry analogously suppresses hole wave functions. Using a finite-difference effective-mass framework, we identify three excitonic states in CdS/ZnSe quantum dots: a weakly confined state, a Casimir-like state in which the intercore gap suppresses the hole wave function by analogy with conducting plates in the Casimir effect, and a bonding state with intercore hole delocalization. Energy-distance analysis reveals a characteristic intercore gap where the Casimir-like force vanishes, marking the attractive-repulsive transition. The exciton binding energy remains nearly invariant across all three states, contrasting with single-core QDs where it varies streriously. These results establish intercore geometry as an effective degree of freedom for exciton engineering in multicore quantum dot architectures.
n48b394b4e712: Nanoparticle-based combination therapy suffers poor spatiotemporal coordination from mismatched drug release. Herein, we report a poly(l-glutamic acid) (PLG) nanosystem that exploits distinct ester hydrolysis kinetics of a vascular-disrupting agent (combretastatin A4, CA4) and a hypoxia-responsive prodrug (imidazoquinoline azide, IMDQ-N3) for spatiotemporal coordination, while incorporating antigen-capturing moieties to enhance immune responses. Importantly, to overcome the limitations of conventional labeling methods, which only track the nanocarrier backbone and are prone to false-positive results, we developed a label-free, dual-extraction LC-MS/MS workflow to distinguish free from conjugated drugs, revealing the in vivo fate and providing direct quantitative validation of our kinetic design at the drug level. Our results show that free drugs accounted for only 4.6% and 0.2% of total circulating drugs, markedly reducing toxicity. The optimized formulation achieved spatiotemporally coordinated differential release and activation within tumors. This synergistic kinetic design and novel analytics provide a design paradigm and validation tool for PLG-based combination therapy.
n01083b68649e: Coupled Chern layers can realize axion insulators, but topological gap retention and spin-selective hinge control remain material challenges. We propose a material-design strategy using inversion-symmetric half-Chern layers, exemplified by an antiferromagnetic Ni2I2 stack. Opposite odd-Chern layers at inequivalent inversion embeddings fix an axionic decoupled reference. Interlayer-centered parity–time symmetry and half-Chern spin selectivity help retain the layer-derived gap upon coupling. First-principles calculations predict an axion insulator with a 163 meV bulk gap. A material-informed model shows how interlayer coupling gaps the Chern-layer edge-state manifold, leaving termination-dependent chiral hinge channels. Reversing transverse canting relocates a hinge channel and reverses its propagation while retaining the dominant longitudinal-spin sign inherited from its terminal layer. Layer parity selects relative hinge arrangements and spin sectors, enabling coordinated control of position, chirality, and longitudinal spin.
ned06259f57fc: While sonodynamic therapy (SDT) holds promise for localized tumor ablation, its ability to elicit systemic antitumor immunity remains inadequate due to weak immunogenic priming. Herein, we report a dual-engine single-atom-engineered nanoplatform (MNSe) that converts SDT into a robust immunological reprogrammer via irreversible mitochondrial sabotage. By tuning the central heteroatom of an isoindigo derivative, selenium substitution significantly amplifies spin–orbit coupling, maximizing ultrasound-triggered reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Conjugation with a triphenylphosphonium moiety precisely localizes this amplified oxidative stress to mitochondria. Rationally coupling atom-enhanced ROS with precise subcellular targeting effectively exceeds the biological damage threshold and overcomes endogenous repair mechanisms. The resulting organelle disruption triggers substantial cytosolic leakage of mitochondrial DNA to robustly activate the cGAS-STING pathway. In vivo, this drives interferon-β secretion and CD8+ T-cell infiltration to inhibit primary and distant tumors and to establish durable immunological memory against tumor recurrence, providing a powerful paradigm for spatiotemporally controllable cancer immunotherapy.
nbb225b6c2e6e: Lipid nanoparticles modified with hydroxyzine, an antihistamine compound active in the central nervous system, enable brain delivery of mRNA and gene-editing components in multiple animal models.
n45728374feac: Ptychographic atomic electron tomography determines the 3D positions of 6,648 individual carbon atoms in twisted bilayer graphene with 0.12 Å precision, revealing stacking-dependent corrugations and chiral lattice distortions resembling merons and anti-skyrmions.
n27e93fa2b723: Applied potentials can alter heterogeneous catalysis, but the roles of ions, solvent, and reactants at the polarized catalyst-electrolyte interface remain unclear. Here, we track potential-driven interfacial mass redistribution during aqueous Pd-catalyzed alkynol semi-hydrogenation using an operando electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance (EQCM). By combining gravimetric measurements with a volumetric occupancy model, we quantify the competitive redistribution of ions, reactants, and hydrogen at the solid-liquid interface. The results show that hydrated Na+ promotes cathodic interfacial mass accumulation, forming a cation-bridged microenvironment that enriches alkynol and limits H2 availability. Positive polarization disrupts this microenvironment, promotes product removal, and restores surface hydrogen. Based on these results, we developed an oscillating potential program (100 s at –0.9 V, 20 s at +0.5 V) to control reactant enrichment, product removal, and hydrogen availability, increasing alkenol selectivity from ∼50% to 97% while enhancing activity by 173%.
nb06f4a8a76c1: Decarboxylative protonation/deuteration provides a powerful strategy for removing carboxylic acid handles and installing C–H/D bonds. However, existing catalytic methods typically rely on separate components to conduct the necessary proton-transfer, electron-transfer, and hydrogen-atom-transfer steps, restricting substrate scope and scalability. Herein we report a single-catalyst platform for decarboxylative protonation/deuteration that is broadly tolerant of carboxylic acids and readily scalable to 100 mmol in flow. Diarylquinoline organocatalysts function simultaneously as the base, photo-oxidant, and hydrogen-atom donor, demonstrating an underexplored reactivity mode for photocatalysts in which reductive quenching occurs by facilitating C–H bond formation rather than conventional electron transfer processes. Mechanistic studies indicate that oxidation is achieved through proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET), resulting in high chemoselectivity for carboxylic acid activation. Hammett analysis reveals that catalyst electronics strongly influence the reaction rate, and an uncommon inverse kinetic isotope effect provides evidence for a turnover-limiting, hydrogen-bonded transition state. Finally, reactivity can be diverted toward decarboxylative oxidation to form carbonyl compounds simply by changing the reaction atmosphere, offering versatile synthetic control.
n58d4fa2c7544: Liquid metals often exhibit enhanced catalytic performance owing to their inherent characteristics, including the facile preparation of liquid alloys, atomic dispersion of dissolved elements, high-entropy surface structures, adaptive atomic configurations, and resistance to coking. These features fundamentally distinguish liquid metals from their solid counterparts, which possess fixed atomic arrangements. The transient geometries and electronic properties of liquid atoms within a dynamic matrix increase the possibility to align with various reactants, enabling energy-favorable adsorption patterns and reaction pathways. The catalytic properties of liquid media can be tuned by regulating the dissolved components and/or combining with other functional species. To date, a variety of bond dissociation and formation reactions, centering on C–C, C–H, C–O, C=C, C–N, and C–Cl, have been achieved using liquid metal media. The distinctive catalytic phenomena and the underlying mechanisms associated with liquid metals challenge the conventional understanding of catalysis based on solid-state catalysts. The use of liquid metal media for chemical reactions remains at an early stage, offering great opportunities for future exploration.
nb567c17ed8b9: Although γ-Al2O3-supported Pt–Sn catalysts are central to industrial propane dehydrogenation (PDH), conventional support design has primarily focused on structural properties, largely overlooking the role of surface hydroxyl chemistry in governing metal–support interactions. Here, we show that the distribution of surface hydroxyl types strongly affects Pt–Sn anchoring, particle growth, and performance of the catalyst supported on γ-Al2O3. By hydrothermally tailoring AlOOH precursors and exploiting a topotactic phase transition, three γ-Al2O3 supports (Al2O3-AIP, Al2O3-NP, and Al2O3-NF) with distinct distributions of terminal μ1-OH and doubly bridged μ2-OH sites were prepared. Systematic characterization showed that the hydroxyl-rich Al2O3-NP and Al2O3-NF supports produced substantially smaller Pt–Sn particles than Al2O3-AIP. Spectroscopic trends suggest preferential involvement of acidic μ1-OH sites at lower precursor loadings and progressively greater involvement of μ2-OH sites as the μ1-OH sites approached saturation. The μ2-OH-enriched surfaces favored precursor anchoring associated with highly dispersed Pt–Sn clusters (∼0.6 nm) after reduction. In propane dehydrogenation at 580 °C, the μ2-OH-enriched 0.5Pt–1.3Sn/Al2O3-NF catalyst achieved an initial propane conversion of 60% while maintaining a propylene selectivity above 97%. Site-occupancy experiments and C3H6-DRIFTS further suggest that precursor anchoring involving μ2-OH sites is associated with improved Pt–Sn dispersion and weaker propylene adsorption. These results show that controlling surface hydroxyl types can regulate metal anchoring and particle growth in Al2O3-supported dehydrogenation catalysts.
nea087f14cc45: Mathematical modeling provides a powerful framework for understanding and mitigating degradation in catalyst materials such as platinum nanoparticles. A hallmark of platinum degradation during voltage cycling is the appearance of two distinct maxima in the dissolved Pt concentration: a smaller peak upon increasing potential and a larger peak upon decreasing potential. To explain this observation, we propose a kinetic multi-reaction model of Pt nanoparticle oxidation and dissolution, which describes dissolution as an interplay between direct electrochemical dissolution, passivation of the Pt surface, and the electrochemical dissolution of Pt oxides. The model is calibrated using cyclic voltammograms and time traces of Pt ion concentrations measured for two Pt catalyst samples with different nanoparticle sizes and different supports (carbon-supported 3 nm and unsupported 30 nm particles). The model results show very good agreement with the experimental data and indicate that the dissolution dynamics are indeed governed by oxide surface passivation and dissolution. Furthermore, comparison of results for different catalysts shows that the observed differences in Pt dissolution arise not only from variations in reaction rates on particles of different sizes but also from differences in the catalysts’ microscopic structure, which significantly influence Pt loss through diffusion.
n525ad58bd624: Understanding the role of low-valent cobalt species in cross-coupling catalysis remains a central challenge, particularly in distinguishing two-electron organometallic pathways from radical-based mechanisms. Herein, we report the isolation and comprehensive characterization of cobalt(II) and cobalt(I) intermediates supported by a tetradentate diazapyridinophane (tBuN4) ligand and elucidate their roles in Kumada cross-coupling reactions. Structural, spectroscopic, and computational studies reveal partial ligand-centered reduction in the “Co(I)” species, which function as single-electron initiators for halogen atom transfer from aryl bromides. Mechanistic investigations suggest that the resulting aryl radicals follow two distinct pathways: solvent-mediated hydrogen atom transfer leading to protodehalogenation, or interception by Grignard reagents to form C(sp2)–C(sp2) bonds through an SRN1-type mechanism (radical-nucleophilic aromatic substitution). Overall, these findings establish a radical-mediated framework for Co-catalyzed Kumada coupling and highlight ligand denticity as a key factor in governing reaction pathways.
n2342929d41a8: Hydrocracking of polyolefin waste into liquid fuels over bifunctional catalysts requires efficient synergy between metal sites for H2 activation and acid sites for C–C bond cleavage. However, on nonzeolitic, oxide-based supports, these two functionalities are typically distributed in a random manner, limiting their spatial proximity and, consequently, the overall catalytic efficiency. Herein, we report an interface-design strategy that enforces nanoscale spatial coupling between metal and acid sites within a single structural unit, specifically tailored for polyolefin hydrocracking. The catalyst comprises highly dispersed rhodium (Rh) species anchored on an amorphous NbOx-doped γ-Al2O3 support. The amorphous Nb–O–Al interfaces generate electron-deficient Nb centers that function as medium-strong Lewis acid sites, while simultaneously modulating the electronic and coordination environment of the adjacent Rh species responsible for H2 activation. The nanoscale proximity of these complementary sites facilitates the coupling of acid-mediated C–C bond transformation with the subsequent hydrogenation of reactive intermediates. When applied to the hydrocracking of low-density polyethylene under mild conditions (240 °C, 2 MPa H2), the optimized Rh/10Nb–Al catalyst achieves a liquid product space-time yield of 283 gliquid·gmetal–1·h–1 with a methane selectivity of only 0.77%. Quantitative analysis reveals a linear correlation between the density of these interfacial strong Lewis acid sites and the hydrocracking activity, thereby directly linking the catalytic performance to the interfacial structure. This study establishes interfacial engineering as a rational strategy to encode metal–acid intimacy into the catalyst architecture, thereby offering a general design principle for selective plastic-to-fuel conversion.
n16220f3a2062: The development of high-efficiency NH3 synthesis catalysts under mild conditions is urgently required to alleviate the excessive energy consumption and carbon emissions in traditional Haber–Bosch processes. Although Ru-based catalysts show considerable potential, their catalytic activity is often severely constrained by hydrogen poisoning caused by strong H2 adsorption. Herein, we report the fabrication of a Ba/0.1Re–Ru/AC catalyst through the strategic integration of single-atom Re species into a conventional Ba/Ru/AC framework. Notably, the Ba/0.1Re–Ru/AC catalyst exhibits a high NH3 synthesis rate of 65.1 mmol g–1 h–1 at 400 °C and 1 MPa. Mechanistic investigations reveal that single-atom Re species function as a supplementary active site for H2 adsorption and activation. The incorporation of Re also facilitates H-spillover over the catalyst surface, which effectively alleviates the competitive adsorption between H2 and N2 on Ru sites and consequently mitigates hydrogen poisoning on Ru nanoclusters. Concurrently, the incorporation of single-atom Re modulates the defect density of the support and promotes the creation of additional strong Lewis basic sites. These structural changes induce a strong electronic metal–support interaction (EMSI) effect, which specifically tunes the electronic structure of the Ru nanoclusters. This synergistic interplay between single-atom Re sites and Ru nanoclusters establishes a compelling paradigm for the rational design of highly efficient NH3 synthesis catalysts.
n79d26d1e8ae9: The rate-determining step (RDS), which determines rate capability in lithium-rich manganese-based oxide (LRMO) cathode materials, remains unclear. In this work, we establish a quantitative diagnostic method for the RDS in LRMOs using in-situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) at different states of charge (SOC) and C-rates. From our results, the SOC determines the intrinsic bottleneck of the RDS, while the C-rate drives the transition from single-step to mixed control. Upon discharging to 4.4 V, the RDS is dominated by electron transfer at the interface accompanied by layered-to-spinel phase transition, whereas it is strongly influenced by solid-state diffusion in the bulk with depletion of Li vacancies arising from Jahn–Teller distortion when discharging to 3.0 V. Furthermore, Li+ diffusion, instead of charge transfer, plays a major part in the RDS of LRMOs when the C-rates are increased. These findings establish quantitative criteria for designing future cathode materials.
n929edd1b75c4: Ultraviolet (UV) radiation in sunlight is well known to harm components of solar modules, especially those of emerging photovoltaic technologies. Current accelerated UV tests, however, differ in spectral range and by orders of magnitude in intensity and dose. Their usual anchors, IEC 61215-2 preconditioning at 15 kW h m–2 and a fixed UV fraction of AM1.5G, do not represent long-term outdoor exposure. Here, we quantify annual outdoor UV doses (280–400 nm) across the contiguous United States from the National Solar Radiation Database for horizontal, fixed-tilt, and tracked mounting. Spectroradiometer measurements at two sites validate the model. Annual horizontal-plane doses span 72–133 kW h m–2, with a median of nearly 100 kW h m–2, so IEC 61215-2 preconditioning simulates only 1.4–2.5 months of outdoor exposure. Single-axis and dual-axis tracking typically add 10 and 18 kW h m–2, respectively. Finally, we propose reporting the source spectrum and expressing the test dose as a multiple of the annual outdoor dose for a stated location and mounting.
nd19a205d0334: Nickel oxides are among the most active electrocatalysts for the alkaline oxygen evolution reaction (OER), a key process in green hydrogen production. However, the fundamental reaction mechanism remains unclear, limiting the rational design of electrocatalysts capable of reducing the cost of sustainable hydrogen generation. Herein, we develop an air-stable model electrocatalyst system of submonolayer nickel oxide (NiO) nanosheets with controlled coverages and morphologies on atomically flat Au(111), enabling atomic-scale investigation of structure–activity relationships under ambient conditions. Atomic force microscopy (AFM), scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) in ultrahigh vacuum (UHV), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and electrochemical measurements were combined to correlate nanosheet structure and composition with electrocatalytic performance. We reveal OER activity scales with nanosheet edge density, identifying edge sites as the dominant active sites of the reaction. XPS measurements demonstrate the formation of nickel hydroxide on the nanosheet surfaces and edges following OER testing, consistent with the generation of a catalytically active nickel oxyhydroxide phase during operation. These findings provide insight into the structure–activity relationships governing NiO electrocatalysts and demonstrate a strategy for resolving atomic-scale structure–activity relationships without the need to maintain samples under UHV. We propose that future NiO-based OER electrocatalysts are designed to maximize the number density of accessible edge sites, hence maximizing the electrocatalytic activity.
nbb19243ce8a1: Organic molecules with high redox potentials and large theoretical capacities are promising cathode materials for aqueous zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs). However, their practical application is hindered by issues of dissolution, low electrical conductivity, and insufficient utilization of active sites. We report herein freestanding film cathodes for high-performance ZIBs with superior charge storage and heat management, wherein a meticulously designed bipolar redox molecule is assembled into a continuous three-dimensional conductive framework of MXene-bonded single-walled carbon nanotubes. The optimal cathode-based coin cells deliver the highest specific capacity of 406.6 mAh g–1 at 0.05 A g–1 and an initial capacity of 219.61 mAh g–1 at 10 A g–1 with extraordinary cycling stability over 60,000 cycles with an average capacity decay of only 2.5 × 10–4% per cycle. Further cycling test at 55 °C and 3 A g–1 reveals an initial capacity of 252.15 mAh g–1 with over 82.75% retention after 3000 cycles and ∼100% coulombic efficiency. Importantly, thermal conductivity and infrared thermal imaging were employed for clear elaboration of temperature evolution dynamics and thermal distribution under different electrode structures. Our work correlating the structure design and thermal management of electrodes provides insights for the rational design of high-performance ZIBs.
na48a6f98f21f: Active tuning of the spectral response within sensing materials is critical for application-specific optoelectronics. However, current approaches typically suffer from limited tunability, complex architectures, or sacrificed stability. Here we report an on-chip cation intercalation strategy that transforms the Kitaev-candidate Mott insulator α-ruthenium chloride (α-RuCl3) into a tetramethylammonium (TMA+)-intercalated RuCl3 layered superlattice. The intercalation-induced reconstruction of the Mott-derived electronic states substantially narrows the optical gap from ∼1.1 eV to ∼0.6 eV, extending the spectral response into the short-wave infrared (SWIR) regime. The introduction of an in situ van der Waals tunneling barrier suppresses dark current by >3 orders of magnitude and enhances specific detectivity by 4–6 orders of magnitude. By employing machine learning models, we demonstrate device-response-guided image processing for intelligent recognition under degraded environments. This work establishes a connection between correlated-electron systems and intelligent sensing, stimulating research directions at the intersection of quantum materials, optoelectronics, and intelligent sensing systems.
n6f61e75fcb12: Controlling the interplay between reduction and galvanic processes is critical for tailoring the structure and composition of multimetallic nanocrystals. Here, we report a synthetic strategy to produce anisotropic Au–Pd–Pt nanocrystals with tunable morphologies and elemental distributions. Platinum deposition on single-crystal Au@Pd nanorods (NRs) was modulated by varying the concentration of ascorbic acid, enabling control over the balance between reduction and galvanic-like processes. This approach yields distinct nanostructures, including nanoframes, cloud-like morphologies, and core–shell–shell architectures. Advanced electron microscopy, including high-resolution HAADF STEM imaging, EDX elemental mapping, and electron tomography, reveals intricate elemental distributions, the formation of cavities and tunnels, the apparent preservation of single-crystal characteristics in Au@Pd NRs under the explored conditions, and gold etching induced by the platinum precursor. A preliminary evaluation of catalytic activity suggests enhanced ethanol oxidation performance for nanoframe structures. These findings establish a versatile strategy for engineering anisotropic multimetallic nanocrystals through controlled redox interplay.
nea9a03d80977: Aquatic foods provide around 15% of consumed animal-derived protein worldwide and aquaculture now supplies most of it. But the industry faces significant challenges in disease prevention and excessive use of antimicrobials. Vaccination, particularly for juvenile fish, can mitigate these risks, but manual and automated needle-based vaccination methods are costly, stressful, and labor-intensive. Here, a water-resistant, food-grade microneedle platform is designed to deliver cargos underwater. Silk fibroin-based microneedles are engineered to remain water resistant from minutes to hours in order to penetrate fish skin in wet conditions. To meet the requirements of different underwater applications, three microneedle morphologies─shell, solid-tip, and hollow─are developed, and their different combinations of mechanical integrity, water-resistance performance, cargo compatibility, and release kinetics are studied. The microneedles also preserve the supercoiled conformation of ⩾50% of the loaded pIHNVw-G plasmids─developed to protect fish against infectious hematopoietic necrosis virus─outside the cold chain for 4 weeks under dry conditions. In pilot animal studies, injected microneedles remain attached to zebrafish and juvenile rainbow trout while swimming. Using this food-based microneedle platform, we envision the development of tools for underwater vaccination of juvenile fish that increase aquaculture efficiencies and reduce environmental impact.
nfdc98ccc5673: When early intermediates begin to bias subsequent pathways during protein self-assembly remains difficult to resolve experimentally because early-stage processes are transient and poorly accessible. Here, using regenerated silk fibroin as a model system, we experimentally capture and analyze an early nucleation window in which assembly pathways begin to diverge before conformational locking occurs. By combining controlled electric-field perturbation with multiscale structural characterization and coarse-grained simulations, we identify reproducible nanoscale intermediates that mediate pathway selection. Within this window, electric fields bias early assembly kinetics in a nonmonotonic manner, modulating the formation, elongation, and competition of intermediates rather than directly enforcing structure or orientation. Time-resolved measurements show that subsequent growth proceeds primarily through elongation and fusion of existing intermediates, while β-sheet formation and crystallization emerge only at later stages and serve to stabilize pathways that were biased at earlier stages. Together, we locate the emergence of detectable pathway biasing within the nucleation stage and provide a framework for understanding and guiding protein self-assembly under nonequilibrium conditions.
n0ac8088f8a14: Melanoma treatment remains limited by drug resistance, immune-related adverse effects, and inadequate tumor-specific drug delivery. Nanoparticle (NP)-based delivery platforms have shown promise, but their clinical translation is hindered by rapid immune clearance and suboptimal biocompatibility. Current membrane-coating strategies often depend on invasive cell sources and lack patient-specific applicability. This study introduces a personalized melanoma therapy platform that integrates MnO2 NPs (MNPs) coated with urine-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) membranes into a hydrogel-based transdermal patch. The patient-derived iPSC membrane enhances tumor targeting and immune evasion through the CXCR4/CXCL12 axis, while the MNPs facilitate pH-responsive release of cytotoxic drugs within the tumor microenvironment, maximizing therapeutic efficacy. The hydrogel transdermal patch enables direct, noninvasive delivery to skin lesions, promoting sustained drug exposure and potentially improving patient compliance. By combining autologous cell membrane coating, pH-responsive nanocarriers, and transdermal administration, this platform addresses key limitations of current melanoma therapies and supports the potential for clinical translation of personalized nanomedicine.
n128043b4e252: Inflammatory breast cancer (IBC) is a highly aggressive breast cancer subtype characterized by diffuse, biologically invasive growth and poorly defined tissue boundaries, resulting in a high mortality rate even after multimodal treatment. Here, we report an intracellular polymerization-induced self-assembly (PISA) strategy that constructs mechanically active peptide nanosheets. Upon 365 nm UV irradiation, the photoinitiator Irgacure 2959 (I2959) initiates intracellular PISA of HisMAm in IBC cells. The corresponding nanosheets prepared in vitro exhibit a thickness of ∼30 nm and a wet-state apparent Young’s modulus of 8.02 ± 0.43 MPa. These nanosheets act through two coordinated materials-cell interactions: (i) increasing cellular viscosity and spatially associating with the actin cytoskeleton, suppressing cell migration and invasion; and (ii) accumulating in the endoplasmic reticulum and eliciting paraptosis-like cell death. In a subcutaneous IBC xenograft model, localized fiber-assisted light activation achieves 72.2% tumor growth inhibition without overt systemic toxicity. Overall, this work establishes intracellular PISA as a spatiotemporally controlled materials strategy for localized IBC treatment.
ne9f28e2a842a: Nanotechnology-integrated diagnostic platforms are increasingly being developed across infectious disease management, from screening and diagnosis to potentially treatment-guiding assessment and monitoring. Yet current progress has rarely been synthesized from a clinical management perspective, making it difficult to determine which technologies are ready for decentralized use, where progress remains fragmented, and which clinical needs remain unmet. This review examines nanotechnology-enabled strategies according to how they enable the sample-to-answer workflow, rather than classifying them by material type. Major diagnostic platform architectures are then assessed in terms of practical implementation, with emphasis on platform-specific limitations and emerging solutions. Current applications are further mapped across the infectious disease management continuum to identify established capabilities, missing links, and disconnects from clinical workflows. The broader changes needed to close these gaps are also discussed. This review aims to clarify how nanotechnology-integrated diagnostic platforms can be better developed toward decentralized, reliable, and clinically actionable infectious disease management.
n358cc72210ca: Light-matter interactions provide a powerful route to dynamically control ferroelectricity in low-dimensional materials, yet the microscopic mechanisms governing light-induced polarization remain elusive in sliding ferroelectrics. However, the influence of photodoped carriers on the macroscopic polarization and lattice responses remains largely unexplored. In this work, we employ first-principles calculations to demonstrate the microscopic origin of the photostrictive response in rhombohedral bilayer MoS2 under carrier photodoping. The system exhibits a characteristic lattice deformation, including in-plane expansion with the magnitude of 2% under a moderate photodoping density, collectively enhancing electronic hybridization. The coupling gives rise to a substantial interlayer contraction and an increase in out-of-plane spontaneous polarization, accompanied by a softening of the interlayer vibrational mode. These results demonstrate a microscopic, nonthermal pathway for modulating ferroelectric properties and underscore the potential of lattice-engineered polarization control in two-dimensional sliding ferroelectrics for advanced optoelectronic and information storage technologies.
n36da251f480f: Two-dimensional polymers (2DPs) integrate the molecular programmability of synthetic polymers with the reduced dimensionality and surface accessibility of atomically thin materials. Realizing their functional potential and establishing reliable structure–property relationships, however, require precise control over lattice topology, crystallinity, orientation, thickness, and defect structure. Interfacial polymerization is particularly suited to this objective because interfaces confine network formation while regulating molecular organization, reactant transport, bond-formation kinetics, nucleation, crystal growth, and defect evolution. This Review summarizes the molecular design principles underlying interfacial 2DP synthesis and compares four major environments according to whether polymerization occurs at a liquid or solid surface: air–liquid, liquid–liquid, solid–liquid, and vapor–solid interfaces. We contrast liquid surfaces, which couple dynamic confinement with transport-regulated molecular reorganization and scalable film growth, with solid surfaces, which provide adsorption, templating, and catalytic control while enabling direct mechanistic investigation at the molecular scale. We further examine how precursor organization, mass transport, crystallization pathways, stacking, and defect evolution collectively determine the structural quality of 2DPs. Particular attention is given to mechanistic insights from advanced characterization methods that directly track nucleation and domain-growth dynamics and resolve grain-boundary and defect structures from molecular to atomic resolution. Emerging electronic and stimuli-responsive devices are discussed to illustrate how framework design, structural quality, and interfacial organization translate into functional performance. Finally, we identify opportunities to advance interfacial polymerization from empirical optimization toward predictive synthesis that bridges local atomic precision with macroscopic structural uniformity.
ne148b7a8a3e5: Combining high mechanical strength, fatigue resistance, and reprocessability in a single soft material remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report a strategy based on spatially decoupled interparticle hydrogen bonding in architecturally controlled brush particle blends. Complementary hydrogen-bonding motifs, namely poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) as donor and poly(dimethylaminoethyl methacrylate) (PDMAEMA) as acceptor, were incorporated into poly(n-butyl acrylate) (PnBA)-based gradient brush particles via surface-initiated atom transfer radical polymerization (SI-ATRP). Upon blending, reversible interparticle hydrogen bonds were formed, functioning as dynamic physical cross-links. The resulting materials exhibited tensile strengths up to 18 MPa, Young’s modulus of 95 MPa, and fracture strains exceeding 150–200%, a combination rarely achieved in physically cross-linked polymer networks. Hierarchical viscoelastic analysis revealed that the synergy between reversible interparticle bonding and architectural heterogeneity generates broad relaxation spectra and multiscale energy dissipation pathways. These features collectively underpin outstanding fatigue resistance, crack-propagation suppression, reprocessability, and thermally assisted self-healing, with annealing at 50 °C restoring approximately 90% of the original modulus and near-complete tensile strength. This work establishes spatial decoupling of hydrogen-bond donors and acceptors as a transferable design principle for durable, recyclable structural soft materials.
n7a7fc02a1930: Halide solid-state electrolytes have emerged as promising candidates for all-solid-state lithium batteries due to their high oxidative stability and deformability, yet their moderate ionic conductivity remains a bottleneck. While incorporating ionically insulating ZrO2 nanoparticles has been experimentally shown to enhance the ionic conductivity of Li2ZrCl6, the atomistic origin governing this interfacial phenomenon remains unclear. Here, we bridge the spatiotemporal gap in modeling complex heterostructures by developing an accurate machine-learned force field based on the neuroevolution potential, enabling large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of ZrO2/Li2ZrCl6 heterostructures. By systematically investigating four representative low-lattice-mismatch ZrO2/Li2ZrCl6 interfaces, we identify spontaneous interfacial amorphization driven by space-charge effects upon surface cleavage, trapping Li+ and leading to under-coordinated Li+ polyhedra with pronounced geometric distortion. These distorted amorphous interfacial regions exhibit markedly enhanced Li+ hopping activity, significantly outperforming the bulk lattice, provided that the local mobile Li+ density is not depleted by surface charge redistribution. This work establishes a computational framework for training validated machine-learned force fields for interfaces and provides one plausible origin for the experimentally observed conductivity boost in the insulator-conductor composites, guiding the rational design of electrolytes toward next-generation solid-state batteries.
n1137f72cffea: It is extremely challenging to clarify the precise atomic-level evolution of nanoclusters from a dynamically trapped state to a thermodynamically selected product. Various factors play distinctly different roles in the thermodynamic and kinetic control of structural transformation reactions. In this study, we used the system Ag14(SPh)12(DPPH)4 → Ag23(SPh)18(DPPH)4 as a homologous model system, and combined single-crystal structural analysis, time-resolved electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS), ultraviolet–visible absorption spectroscopy, and photoluminescence measurements for correlation analysis. Crystallographic studies revealed that the Ag23 framework could be geometrically decomposed into two substructures related to Ag14, both sharing the metal and thioimine groups, providing a structural basis for the bimolecular fusion hypothesis. Time-dependent spectroscopic techniques revealed the consumption process of Ag14 and the growth process of Ag23, while temperature-dependent experiments showed a kinetic window within which the conversion rate accelerated, but higher thermal input would promote breakage/decomposition and form Ag10. Due to the ability of ESI-MS to generate gas-phase fragments, ions containing Ag5- and Ag9 were regarded as candidate species detected by ESI, rather than confirmed solution intermediates. Therefore, the core breakthrough was not the isolated Ag14 or Ag23 nuclear numbers, but the mechanistic connection of the two structurally similar cluster states in a single reaction network and the identification of thermal activation as the key factor guiding the evolution of the cluster states.
ne053ce2870b1: Sodium-metal batteries are promising for low-temperature energy storage, yet conventional electrolytes suffer from an intrinsic trade-off between thermodynamic stability and kinetic transport, causing salt precipitation and solvation collapse. Herein, an asymmetric cooperative solvation structure (ACSS) is introduced to spatially decouple these conflicting requirements via coordination competition between a strong solvating solvent (diethylene glycol dimethyl ether, DME) and a weak solvating (diethylene glycol diethyl ether, DEE). The DME-rich inner core forms compact ternary coordination clusters with Na+ and anions (PF6 −/BF4 −), ensuring enthalpic stability and high salt solubility via geometric ion confinement, while the DEE-rich outer shell sustains entropic mobility through rapid ligand exchange, facilitating hopping transport and lowering desolvation barriers. This enthalpy–entropy compensation preserves ionic conductivity and structural integrity below −40°C. High anion occupancy within the stable clusters promotes preferential anion reduction, yielding an inorganic-rich SEI with high mechanical modulus and low Na+ migration energy, effectively suppressing dendrite growth and interfacial polarization. Consequently, Na||Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 pouch cell achieves a capacity retention of 94% at −40°C. Scaled-up 1.2 Ah hard carbon||Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 and 1.2 Ah hard carbon||NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 pouch cells sustain 400 and 550 cycles at −30°C and −20°C, respectively, demonstrating the promising practical applicability of this electrolyte design.
nc3eb40f8b27d: Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries show great potential for large‐scale energy storage; however, dendrites formation and corrosion on zinc anodes significantly hinder their practical applications. Uneven Zn deposition leads to dendrite growth, while H2O molecules in solvated Zn2+ ions exacerbate surface corrosion and the hydrogen evolution reaction. Herein, we propose a Schiff‐base‐covalently‐grafted UiO‐66‐NH2 metal‐organic framework to construct a bifunctional interface for stable zinc metal anodes. Specifically, the chemical chelation between Schiff base and Zn2+ accelerates desolvation and suppresses side reactions. Meanwhile, the uniformly distributed Zn2+‐chelated sites and the well‐defined confined pore channels of UiO‐66‐NH2 scaffold guide a homogeneous Zn2+ flux and promote Zn(002)‐oriented deposition. As a result, this bifunctional interface enables Zn plating/stripping with a high Coulombic efficiency of 99.8% over 2000 cycles at 5 mA cm−2/1 mAh cm−2. Furthermore, it achieves a capacity retention of over 90% after 4000 charge–discharge cycles in a Zn||MnO2 full cell. This work is expected to open a new avenue for interfacial chemical regulation toward stabilizing zinc metal anodes.
nca95faab8d68: Ocean, as a vast natural reservoir of ionic minerals, provides a promising approach to offset the high cost of hydrogen production from electrocatalytic water splitting. However, the complex ionic environment of seawater compels us to separate out scaling-prone ions via cost-effective membrane separation technology, and further separately electrolyze diluted and concentrated seawater to produce H2 and high value-added marine chemical products. We herein apply electrodialysis to separate out divalent cations and produce twofold concentrated seawater and fresh seawater. A decoupled dual-stream seawater electrolysis (DDSE) strategy is designed. The fresh seawater is routed into an alkaline/AEM water electrolyzer to sustain stable H2 evolution. The concentrated seawater is fed into a home-made electrolyzer to produce NaClO and high-purity Mg(OH)2. A scalable non-noble metal-based electrode (50 cm × 50 cm) was designed and fabricated with high activity and stability when applied in the chlorine evolution reaction. System-level evaluation validates the feasibility of the DDSE strategy. Through rigorous techno-economic analysis, the unit price of H2 production is reduced to $0.39 kgH2 −1 (DOE 2030 target: $1 kgH2 −1), and the Global Warming Potential can be reduced up to 6.83%. This proposed DDSE strategy offers a new approach for cost-effective green hydrogen production with comprehensive seawater valorization.
nc4b885ae244f: NH3 is an attractive hydrogen carrier, but efficient H2 release is hindered by N–H bond cleavage and hydrogen poisoning. Herein, we develop Ni nanoparticle‐supported CeO2 (Ni/CeO2) for low‐temperature photothermal NH3 decomposition. Light irradiation is accompanied by the dynamic generation of oxygen vacancies on CeO2, which couple with adjacent Ni sites to form Ce–Ov–Ni motifs, indicating that illumination can regulate the catalyst surface state beyond its thermal contribution. Experiments and DFT calculations indicate that these interfaces create differentiated local environments for NH3 activation and product evolution. Oxygen‐vacancy‐associated sites favor NH3 adsorption, N–H bond activation, and N‐containing intermediates, whereas adjacent Ni sites accommodate H migration and recombination. Moreover, vacancy‐induced electronic modulation weakens H2 adsorption on Ni, thereby facilitating H2 release. Such site differentiation and facilitated hydrogen removal reduce the competitive occupation of active sites by N‐ and H‐containing species and contribute to the resistance to hydrogen poisoning. Under photothermal conditions, 10 wt.% Ni/CeO2 achieves 96.3% NH3 conversion at 450°C, versus 42.5% under thermal catalysis, and maintains >95% conversion at a GHSV of 18,000 mL·gcat−1·h−1. It delivers 20.09 mmol·gcat−1·min−1 H2 with 50 h stability. This work demonstrates light‐induced oxygen‐vacancy–metal interfaces for efficient, hydrogen‐poisoning‐resistant NH3‐to‐H2 conversion.
n1a070a190708: Most electrolyte additives enable long-term Li plating/stripping at <3 mA cm− 2, non-applicable to practical Li-metal batteries (LMBs) operating at ≥5 mA cm− 2 and ≥ 5 mAh cm− 2. Here, we report an interaction chemistry that enables simultaneous solvation and interfacial regulation by exploring a novel N-heterocyclic molecule (i.e., TPTC)—comprising an N-heterocyclic core and four pyridine units–as an efficient additive for achieving ultra-stable Li-metal anodes under practical conditions. Electron-rich N atoms in TPTC serve as ion-dipole interaction sites, inducing competitive coordination that weakens Li+ solvation and enhances Li+ migration in the bulk electrolyte, which homogenizes Li+ concentration near the interface, favoring high-rate Li deposition. TPTC also adsorbs on Li surface to construct a protective layer with a low interfacial de-solvation barrier, which–together with low-barrier Li+ transport through heterocyclic cavities–facilitates uniform Li deposition. Meanwhile, electron-deficient C–H sites in pyridine weakly interact with TFSI−, forming an anion-rich interfacial region that in situ decomposes into an inorganic-rich interphase, affording high-flux Li+ transport. This synergy allows stable Li plating/stripping at 10 mA cm−2/10 mAh cm−2 for 3000 h. Paired with a high-loading LiFePO4 cathode (∼15 mg cm−2) and thin Li (∼100 µm), the cell maintains 87.8% capacity after 400 cycles.
nd3349ddda9be: While dynamic solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) construction and solvation engineering have transformed aqueous zinc-ion batteries, translating these approaches to Organic electrolytes (OE) remains a challenging endeavor due to fundamentally different interfacial environments, solvation thermodynamics, and anion decomposition pathways. Despite providing superior thermodynamic stabilization to Zn anode, OE exhibits low ionic conductivity, thereby limiting operational current densities. Herein, we report the first demonstration of Sn(BF4)2/H2O (SFB) additive integration in a non-flammable trimethyl phosphate (TMP)-ethanol (EtOH) (2:1 v/v) OE to architect a gradient SEI interphase on Zn anodes. The multifunctional integration of SFB facilitates the formation of a Sn-coated Zn surface, a BF4 1−-derived SEI@Zn, and H2O molecules as a proton source, collectively contributing to enhanced capacity. This strategic solvent-salt-metal synergy enables bi-layered interfacial engineering within a single electrolyte system, significantly improving the reversibility and stability of the Zn anode. Consequently, SFB enables a robust SEI, achieving exceptional Zn anode durability (7000 h), high-rate capability (10 mA cm−2), and a high Coulombic efficiency (CE) of 99.8%. Full cells with SFB outperform controls in coin and pouch configurations. Given the rarity of additive(s) in OEs, this study offers a new path to boost stability and lifespan of non-aqueous Zn batteries.
n04f597a6ae5b: With tonnes of battery shredded globally, tracing down pathways in upcycling black mass (BM) as catalysts would be a game changer. Existing unwavering synergic combination of inherent metals and graphite in BM drives this novel objective. Herein, we report the critical role of spent graphite for electrocatalytic water splitting applications by systematic evaluation of diverse NMC, LFP, and LCO BM. The study revealed an interesting pattern, wherein the graphite in BM complemented their impurity flaws by delivering an excellent oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity. Defects, surface activation, structural variation, and metal‐graphite synergism arising from prolonged cycle life served as a serendipitous finding of upcycling BM for OER, despite being loaded with impurities and/or degradation byproducts. Further, among these BM sets, direct upcycling of select graphite‐containing BM via mechanochemical functionalisation aided downsized derivatives delivering an overpotential of 260 mV at 10 mA cm−2, while functionalized graphite via bioleaching BM recorded an overpotential of 249 mV, an epoch‐making record in graphite upcycling. By correlating the overall insights using advanced material, electrochemical characterisation studies, and life cycle analysis, the current study unlocks spent graphite benefits for achieving sustainable energy solutions and beyond.
n2a5b42c5d113: The development of versatile, stable, and cost-effective hole-transport layers (HTLs) is essential for advancing next-generation photovoltaic technologies. Herein, we report a series of phenothiazine-based self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) as HTLs for perovskite and organic solar cells. By systematically tuning the substituents, including unsubstituted phenothiazine (PTZ), dibromo-PTZ (PTZ-diBr), and diacetyl-PTZ (PTZ-diACE), we achieve control over interfacial energetics and surface properties. The dual coordination sites of carbonyl groups and sulfur in PTZ-diACE provide Lewis basic sites that coordinate undercoordinated Pb2 + ions, facilitating passivation at the buried HTL/perovskite interface. Additionally, polar acetyl groups induce interfacial dipoles that reinforce the built-in electric field, promoting efficient hole extraction. Among the series, PTZ-diACE exhibits superior film formation, a deeper HOMO level, and stronger interfacial interactions, resulting in enhanced charge extraction and suppressed nonradiative recombination. Consequently, inverted perovskite solar cells employing PTZ-diACE achieve a power-conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.5% with excellent operational stability, retaining 93% of its initial efficiency after 500 h under the ISOS-D-2I protocol. These advantages extend to organic solar cells, where PTZ-diACE delivers a PCE of 20.4% in D18:L8BO devices and demonstrates compatibility across multiple active layers. This study demonstrates phenothiazine-based SAMs as HTLs and provides design guidelines for efficient, stable interfacial materials.
n1c2a0f0716ae: This study presents a quasi‐solid‐state electrolyte based on zwitterionic thermoplastic polyurethane (QS‐Z‐TPU) for lithium metal batteries. Unlike conventional quasi‐solid polymer electrolytes that mainly serve as passive liquid‐electrolyte reservoirs, QS‐Z‐TPU is designed as an active ion‐regulating matrix via phosphorylcholine‐derived zwitterionic groups in the TPU framework. The resulting electrolyte combines the elasticity and film‐forming capability of TPU with dual‐site ion regulation, where phosphate sites coordinate Li+ while quaternary ammonium and urethane N‐H groups immobilize TFSI− anions. This design enhances electrolyte affinity while suppressing destructive swelling due to ionic crosslinking. QS‐Z‐TPU exhibits high ionic conductivity, a wide electrochemical stability window, and an enhanced Li+ transference number. Machine‐learning‐assisted molecular modeling further reveals that the zwitterionic oligomer stabilizes separated LiTFSI configurations through cooperative Li+ coordination and TFSI− association, substantially reducing the energetic penalty for ion‐pair separation. This regulated ion environment promotes uniform Li+ flux at the lithium metal interface and facilitates the formation of a stable inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase. Consequently, QS‐Z‐TPU enables stable Li plating/stripping and improves the cycling stability and rate capability of LFP|Li full cells, further validated in flexible pouch‐cell demonstrations. These findings highlight zwitterionic molecular engineering as an effective strategy for interface‐stabilizing quasi‐solid electrolytes.
n011ea112125e: Defect chemistry for improving electrochemical potential and structural stability traditionally relies on chemical bonding and charge compensation. However, it reaches a bottleneck when the beneficial defect concentration saturates under the formation‐energy constraint, because defect‐induced lattice stress generally dissipates through volume expansion, obscuring its electrochemical contribution. Herein, we establish a defect‐engineering guide that thermodynamically decouples formation energy to extract an unprecedented stress dimension alongside traditional defect concentrations. Crucially, we develop a stepwise process driven by quantitative ligand‐field and stress descriptors to simultaneously screen both dimensions to their limits. We elucidate how universally expansive electrodes like silicon can maintain structural stability while suppressing passive stress release to mitigate expansion. Furthermore, targeting the extreme archetype of non‐expansive Li4Ti5O12 electrodes, we uncover how confined stress can be transformed into a thermodynamic gain to lower their potentials. Among the 612 dual‐doping configurations, the optimal La‐Zr doping maximizes both the defect concentration and the strain energy, reducing the lithiation potential from 1.55 to 1.00 V (vs. Li/Li+) while preserving intrinsic the zero‐strain characteristic. This work proposes a defect‐engineering guide rooted in a four‐quadrant panorama of thermodynamically decoupled concentration and stress dimensions, breaking optimization bottlenecks by harnessing stress upon formation‐energy‐constrained defect saturation to expand the boundaries of defect chemistry.
nfe3f33869172: Effective management of severe hemorrhages and chronic diabetic wounds requires navigating a contradictory fluidic challenge: efficiently clearing hazardous exudates and pathogens without depleting critical regenerative factors. Conventional dressings rely on non‐selective bulk absorption, inadvertently drawing away essential cellular components along with waste fluids. Herein, we report a compartmentalized sponge that resolves this dilemma through a structurally and electrochemically programmable biological filtration strategy. By embedding a selective membrane between an outward‐facing random‐pore layer and a tissue‐facing aligned‐pore layer, the architecture drives directional outward translocation of plasma and micro‐scale pathogens. Concurrently, it physically traps vital regenerative components, like red blood cells and platelets, thereby accelerating localized coagulation at the tissue interface. To actively address microbial threats, Nb2C/CeO2 (NbCe) heterojunctions are integrated into the matrix. The NbCe energy band structure matches the biological redox potential (BRP) of bacterial respiratory chains, triggering spontaneous interfacial electron efflux that effectively disrupts the microbial electron transport chain (ETC). Synergizing precise physical size‐exclusion with targeted thermodynamic biocatalysis, this sponge reduces hemostasis time and blood loss by ∼80% versus commercial Celox, achieving a 95.1% wound closure rate by day 15. This active‐separation platform offers a programmable biomaterials strategy for full‐process tissue repair.
nefb860a012c4: Bending‐based measurements are widely used to probe flexoelectricity in ferroelectric thin films, but the measured response is often shaped by mechanical boundary conditions beyond the intrinsic flexoelectric coefficient. Here we show that the conducting bottom stack acts as a hidden electromechanical boundary condition in mica‐supported BaTiO3 (BTO) capacitors. Dynamic bending measurements reveal opposite bottom‐layer‐thickness dependences for two‐dimensional and oxide electrodes, while a BTO(001)/LSMO(001)/MoS2/mica hybrid exhibits an intermediate response at the same nominal BTO orientation as the MoS2‐supported films. Interface‐resolved first‐principles calculations show that the hybrid retains a stiff BTO/LSMO contact above substantially more compliant LSMO/MoS2 and MoS2/mica junctions. A reduced shear‐transfer model combines the local interface stiffnesses into an effective interfacial‐path stiffness, and finite‐element simulations confirm progressive suppression of interfacial slip with increasing tangential stiffness. These results identify the complete bottom‐stack shear‐transfer pathway as a mechanical control of bending‐induced polarization and piezoelectric admixture in ferroelectric thin‐film flexoelectric measurements.
n17ea4a81a437: The rapid expansion of renewable energy and electrified systems is increasing the demand for safe, low‐cost, and resource‐sustainable energy storage. Rechargeable zinc‐air batteries are promising because they combine abundant Zn, aqueous electrolytes, and an air‐fed oxygen electrode, yet their long‐term reversibility is constrained by coupled oxygen reactions, Zn chemistry, species transport, interfacial evolution, and finite material inventories. This review develops an operating‐state‐resolved framework linking reaction‐pathway competition during discharge, charge, and rest with shared‐electrolyte transport, electrode reversibility, cross‐component coupling, inventory retention, and device reversibility. An evidence hierarchy distinguishes direct operando or component‐resolved observations from correlation, mechanistic inference, and cross‐system analogy, while practical evaluation is considered under explicit load, Zn utilization, electrolyte inventory, gas environment, cumulative output, maintenance, and failure boundaries. These elements are further integrated into reaction‐selectivity‐oriented cross‐component co‐design. The resulting framework specifies the evidence needed to attribute failure, compares cycling claims within declared load and inventory boundaries, and identifies conditions under which air‐electrode, electrolyte, and Zn‐interface modifications can remain compatible.
n5b43753484cf: Conventional scintillators rely on crystalline lattices that lock luminescent centers into discrete, fixed configurations, fundamentally restricting the dynamic regulation of emission pathways. Here, we establish a strategy for tuning excited‐state behavior in hybrid glass scintillators by harnessing structural disorder as an active design parameter for regulating local Mn coupling environments. Through non‐stoichiometric engineering of hybrid organic–inorganic (methyl(triphenyl)phosphonium)2MnBr4 (MTP2MnBr4) glasses, continuously distributed Mn–Mn coupling environments are established within a single amorphous phase, spanning from isolated Mn monomers to exchange‐coupled pairs. This disorder‐mediated coupling landscape reconstructs the excited‐state hierarchy and facilitates excited‐state energy redistribution, producing continuously tunable luminescence from green to orange‐red under both UV and X‐ray excitation. The optimized glass achieves a light yield of 43 825 photons MeV−1 and spatial resolution of 13.6 lp mm−1, rivaling commercial standards. Leveraging the composition‐dependent emission contrast, flexible glass‐core fibers are fabricated for quantitative ratiometric X‐ray dosimetry, with potential for wearable radiation monitoring. This work establishes disorder engineering as a general strategy for reconstructing local excited‐state configurations beyond the constraints of crystalline symmetry.
n10f9e6a3b367: The relentless demand for data‐intensive computing has exposed the fundamental bottlenecks of the conventional von Neumann architecture, driving the search for alternative processing paradigms. Memristors have emerged as compelling building blocks for next‐generation in‐memory and neuromorphic computing. Within this domain, heterojunction‐based memristors stand out as highly promising candidates, leveraging interfacial engineering to deliver exceptional device performance and multifunctional capabilities. This review provides a comprehensive and critical overview of recent advancements in heterojunction memristors. We systematically examine the material systems, structural classifications, and fabrication strategies that underpin these devices, followed by an in‐depth analysis of their underlying resistive switching (RS) mechanisms. Furthermore, we highlight their transformative potential across diverse application domains, spanning data storage, artificial synapses, neuromorphic biomimetic sensory perception, and advanced logic circuits. Finally, we address the prevailing technical challenges and propose viable strategies, offering a strategic roadmap for the rational design of high‐performance heterojunction memristors to power the future of neuromorphic hardware.
n185812c61b13: Lithium metal stands as the most promising anode material to drive the development of next‐generation energy storage systems owing to its unparalleled theoretical gravimetric capacity. However, the naturally formed solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) is inadequate to suppress the uncontrolled growth of lithium dendrites, posing the safety concerns for lithium metal batteries (LMBs). Herein, we propose a F‐rich Lewis acid metal‐organic framework (F‐mof) as an anion captor and a cation accelerator to mitigate the concentration polarization and expedite the lithium ion transport at anode‐electrolyte interface. The lithiophilic nature of F‐mof with a 3D open framework facilitates the uniform lithium deposition and mitigates the electrode volume change during extended cycling. This strong Lewis acid‐modified Li anode enables Li||Li symmetric cells to achieve an extended cycle life of 2000 h at a high capacity of 2 mAh cm−2. The modified LMBs with LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) cathodes demonstrate the prolonged 700 cycles at 1 C. The NCM811‐pouch cells with a thick cathode (30 mg cm−2) achieve a high energy density of 300 Wh kg−1 based on entire pouch weight. Moreover, this work uses a conversion‐type FeF3 cathode to assemble multilayer pouch cell, achieving a high capacity of 600 mAh for fluoride conversion reaction batteries.
na963c205ebb5: The high‐energy lithium metal battery employing a nonflammable phosphate electrolyte is an attractive strategy to resolve the notorious safety trouble. Unfortunately, the sluggish ion dissociation and transport kinetics, strong interaction of Li+‐phosphates, and uncontrollable secondary reaction between the electrode and electrolyte interfaces severely impedes the cycling stability of lithium metal batteries. Herein, the dual‐function separators with fast ion dissociation and transport capability are designed to enable the homogeneous and efficient ion flux in nonflammable phosphate electrolyte. By virtue of the regulating effect of the designed dual‐function separator, the homogeneous distribution of the ion field and electric field are constructed, thus reducing the concentration polarization among nonflammable phosphate electrolyte and weakening the parasitic reaction of the metallic lithium anode and nickel‐rich cathode with the electrolyte. The Li||Li symmetrical cells exhibit remarkable cycling stability of above 1000 h at 2 mA cm−2. Moreover, the Li||LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) battery exhibits above 90% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 1C. Furthermore, stable bidirectional electrode‐electrolyte interfaces are also realized after cycling. This approach holds great promise for regulating the ion flux in nonflammable electrolyte, and would encourage more separator engineering design to optimize ionic transport behavior.
nd2695f21c233: Lithium dendrite growth represents the primary factor hindering the commercialization of high‐energy‐density lithium metal batteries, as it gives rise to safety hazards and low Coulombic efficiency. Surface morphology of deposited lithium is particularly affected by solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) and current collectors. Herein, we propose a current collector coated by spherical GaIn liquid metal nanoparticles encapsulated in a carbon layer (GaIn@C), which are spontaneously formed by the physical properties of liquid metal. This three‐dimensional spherical GaIn@C layer shows remarkable structure stability and avoids the tip effect during deposition of lithium, thus maintaining a stable residual SEI (rSEI) and dendrite‐free morphology over the repeated plating/stripping processes. The dendrite‐free lithium deposition behavior on GaIn@C layer was revealed via multiphysics simulation, ex‐situ deposition observation, in situ optical experiments, and in situ impedance analysis. Uniform deposition process of lithium half‐cell achieves a cycle life of up to 3500 h at an areal deposition capacity of 5 mAh cm−2. Anode‐free full cell maintains specific capacity of 172.9 mAh g−1 after 100 cycles at 1C, with capacity retention of 99.9% and energy density of pouch battery exceed 410 Wh kg−1. This study presents a general synthetic strategy for the construction of a current collector with stable residual SEI in dendrite‐free lithium metal batteries.
n96686b52d81b: Ferroelastic materials with intrinsically switchable spontaneous strain hold great promise for actuators, shape-memory systems, and energy-harvesting technologies. However, enhancing the Curie temperature (T c) and multifunctionality remain long-standing challenges in hybrid ferroelastics, as the former critically governs the operational temperature window while the latter paves the way for novel functionalities. Here, we present an organic–inorganic hybrid ferroelastic (4-FPD)2KInCl6:Sb (4-FPD = 4-fluoropiperidinium), which showcases remarkable multifunctionality combining a high T c of 417 K with efficient red-light emission. By implementing a fluorination strategy on the parent (piperidinium)2KInCl6 (T c = 263 K), we achieved a record enhancement of 154 K in T c for hybrid metal halide ferroelastics, far exceeding the reported enhancements induced by the isotope effect and other techniques. Moreover, strikingly, isovalent Sb3+ doping into the inorganic framework introduces highly efficient radiative recombination centers within the lattice, which boosts the photoluminescence quantum yield of (4-FPD)2KInCl6 from 2.09% to 85.63% without compromising the intrinsic ferroelastic properties. This study offers an effective route for performance optimization and multifunctional design of hybrid ferroelastics.
n6878b87042ed: In situ polymerization electrolytes hold great promise for high‐energy‐density lithium‐metal batteries but often require additional separators due to their limited mechanical strength. Here, inspired by “glassy gels”, we developed a free‐standing glass gel electrolyte by introducing tributylmethylphosphonium dimethyl phosphate ([P4441] [DMP]) into a poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) matrix. Strong non‐covalent interactions between [P4441] [DMP] and PAA chains generate a tough and homogeneous network while enabling efficient ion transport. The resulting glass gel electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 2.2 mS cm−1, a Li+ transference number of 0.59, a tensile strength of 30 MPa, and an elongation of up to 700%. The solvent‐toughened scaffold effectively confines the liquid electrolyte and mitigates parasitic reactions with Li metal. Consequently, Li||Li symmetric cells achieve stable cycling for 1900 h at 3 mA cm−2 with an areal capacity of 3 mAh cm−2. Li//NCM811 cells retain 90% of their capacity after 420 cycles, while Li//LiCoO2 cells exhibit stable cycling for over 290 cycles at 1 C with a cutoff voltage of 4.6 V. This work provides a robust strategy for designing free‐standing electrolytes for high‐energy‐density lithium‐metal batteries.
n65c1c954b0c0: Stimuli‐responsive luminescent materials offer dynamic optical outputs for advanced information security, yet achieving programmable fluorescence color evolution in water using a single optical input remains challenging. We developed a water‐soluble zwitterionic monomer, 2‐(pent‐4‐en‐1‐yl)isoquinolin‐2‐ium‐5‐sulfonate (IQIS), that exhibits pronounced photofluorochromism under ultraviolet (UV) irradiation. Its fluorescence evolves from blue to green, accompanied by an increase in the overall fluorescence quantum yield from 3.5% to 17.3%. Mechanistic studies reveal that IQIS is weakly pre‐associated in water, while UV irradiation promotes the growth, densification, and packing reorganization of these loose molecular clusters. The resulting long‐wavelength emission exhibits distinct aggregation‐dependent photophysical characteristics and is consistent with an aggregate‐associated excited state with enhanced intermolecular charge‐transfer character. By programming the kinetics of this supramolecular reorganization in different polymeric architectures, high‐resolution grayscale patterns with time‐evolving optical outputs can be generated. Under continuous UV irradiation, the same light used for fluorescence readout simultaneously drives the optical evolution, causing initially visible information to progressively fade and ultimately disappear without an additional stimulus. This single‐input, self‐evolving behavior enables a “Snapchat‐like” transient encryption mode and provides a strategy for spatiotemporal information encoding based on kinetically programmed supramolecular photofluorochromism.
nf4d8d0a9edcb: Residual tumor cells and the immunosuppressive microenvironment caused by incomplete radiofrequency ablation (iRFA) lead to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) recurrence. In this study, HA-V-MTO/LMP@Gel, an injectable sono-piezocatalytic hydrogel, is developed for local treatment of HCC after iRFA. It combines hyaluronic acid-modified, oxygen vacancy-engineered Mn–Ti metal–organic framework nanosheets (HA-V-MTO) with reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive liposomes co-loaded with STING agonist MSA-2 and an anti-PD-1 antibody (LMP) within a thermosensitive chitosan/β-glycerophosphate (CS/β-GP) hydrogel. Oxygen-vacancy engineering lowers the O2 adsorption energy from 0.187 to −2.559 eV and raises the piezoelectric coefficient d 33 from 35.36 to 108.73 pm V−1. Under ultrasound, HA-V-MTO generates ROS through sono-piezocatalysis, with an additional Fenton-like reaction from the Mn-containing framework. The resulting oxidative stress induces mitochondrial injury and promotes cytosolic mtDNA release, thereby facilitating cGAS-mediated STING activation. ROS-mediated LMP destabilization releases MSA-2, which further enhances STING signaling. The hydrogel undergoes temperature-triggered gelation for sustained local release. In a post-iRFA model, HA-V-MTO/LMP@Gel + US raises intratumoral IFN-β 7.9-fold, increases the proportion of mature dendritic cells to 50.8% and that of intratumoral CD8+ T cells to 26.5%, suppresses residual regrowth, prolongs survival, and protects against tumor rechallenge. This work presents a locally retained sono-piezocatalytic system that couples tumor killing with STING-driven immune activation after iRFA.
ne9533fb34810: Spider silk exhibits exceptional mechanical properties, inspiring the development of diverse biomimetic fibers. However, spider silk‐inspired fibers typically introduce β‐sheet‐like domains while neglecting microphase structure regulation, failing to overcome inherent strength‐toughness conflict. Herein, a spider silk‐inspired fiber is fabricated through a microphase engineering strategy by mimicking spidroin assembly process and microphase structure evolution during natural spider silk spinning. Polyurethane (PU) serves as raw material because its molecular structure closely resembles that of nature spidroin's architecture. Through a solvent exchange‐induced phase separation process, the long‐range oriented microphase structures are constructed. The as‐spun fiber achieves a high toughness of 626.14 ± 38.01 MJ m−3, surpassing that of the strongest natural spider silk. Subsequently, post‐treatment is applied to induce crystallization, further increasing the tensile strength to 418.21 ± 9.56 MPa while maintaining a high toughness of 333.09 ± 20.64 MJ m−3. Notably, the spider silk‐inspired fiber can be used as an energy‐absorbing layer in a ballistic board due to its excellent energy dissipation capabilities, reducing deformation by 36.5% compared with a ceramic‐aramid control upon impact with a ∼730 m s−1 bullet. This work highlights the microphase engineering strategy in enhancing mechanical properties of fibers, offering a simple pathway to fabricate high‐performance spider silk‐inspired fibers.
n1b52885c362e: Pericyte loss, an early hallmark of diabetic retinopathy (DR), is linked to hyperglycemia and inflammation, whereas the contribution of mechanical changes in the retina remains unclear. We define design parameters for an iPSC‐derived microphysiological system (MPS) comprising pericyte‐endothelial capillary networks embedded in a dynamically stiffening hydrogel engineered to reproduce matrix stiffening in a controlled, human‐relevant context. Microrheology of Ins2Akita mouse retinas revealed increased storage modulus in perivascular regions at a diabetic timepoint coincident with reduced pericyte coverage and vascular remodeling, establishing a stiffness magnitude used to inform the design of the MPS. In the MPS, progressive matrix stiffening alone, in the absence of hyperglycemic exposure, was sufficient to induce analogous vascular defects and to suppress pericyte expression of NOTCH3, HEY1, JAG1, and N‐cadherin in a focal adhesion kinase (FAK)‐dependent manner. Inhibition of FAK restored pericyte signaling and vascular integrity in stiffened conditions without altering soft controls, identifying a FAK‐dependent mechanotransduction as a druggable target. Single‐cell RNA‐sequencing of human diabetic retinas validated enrichment of focal‐adhesion components and alterations in Notch‐pathway transcripts in pericytes. These findings establish a human MPS showing matrix stiffening as a key regulator of pericyte‐mediated vascular stabilization and nominate it and FAK‐dependent mechanotransduction as targets to prevent DR pathogenesis.
n70fbb8424e77: Burn treatment remains a tough clinical hurdle, as traditional epidermal growth factor (EGF) treatments suffer from rapid proteolytic degradation and poor skin permeation. Herein, a sprayable, multifunctional film (STAR) based on EGFR‐targeting DNA nanoactivators is reported for efficient burn wound healing. The STAR platform combines tannic acid (TA), silk fibroin (SF), and tetrahedral framework nucleic acids (tFNA) modified with tetravalent EGFR‐stimulating aptamers. This design leverages the nanostructure of tFNA to realize multivalent cooperativity, inducing potent and sustained EGFR activation and downstream signaling. Crucially, the ready‐to‐use dual‐component spray formulation offers superior operational convenience compared with conventional hydrogels, ensuring uniform coverage of irregular wounds. Upon co‐spraying, the system rapidly forms a robust, adhesive film in situ, providing an immediate waterproof barrier and localized antimicrobial protection against pathogens. In vitro, STAR significantly enhances the proliferation and migration of keratinocytes and fibroblasts. In vivo, therapeutic efficacy was validated in two distinct models: a full‐thickness scald model and a skin‐grafting model. STAR film exhibited prolonged retention, effectively accelerating re‐epithelialization, promoting organized collagen deposition, and resolving inflammation. Furthermore, STAR enabled suture‐free skin grafting by ensuring stable bio‐adhesion and facilitating bioactive integration at the graft–host interface. This sprayable platform offers a promising strategy for comprehensive burn management and reconstructive surgery.
n2abb4e0fc811: Brain cancer remains a major global health challenge due to its high morbidity and mortality. Current standard therapies are often limited by incomplete tumor resection, systemic toxicity, and the inability to effectively penetrate the blood‐brain barrier (BBB), which restricts drug delivery to the tumor site. These challenges underscore the urgent need for innovative therapeutic strategies that can overcome these barriers and improve treatment outcomes. Biological materials encompass a diverse range of molecules, from small peptides to monoclonal antibodies, either derived from living organisms or synthetically synthesized. Unlike traditional therapies, biologics provide a more targeted approach, including specific tumor targeting, immune system modulation, and regenerating damaged cells. Although biologics offer significant promise for brain cancer treatment, major challenges associated with blood–brain and tumour barriers continue to limit their translation, and comprehensive reviews bridging therapeutic advances with delivery technologies remain scarce. While individual biologic classes have been extensively studied, a unified assessment of these modalities and their delivery optimization is still needed. This review addresses the current gap by critically examining recent advances in biologic therapies and evaluating emerging invasive and non‐invasive delivery strategies to enhance their therapeutic efficacy in brain cancer.
n038bfbc74d13: Electrostatic complex coacervates offer a robust pathway to convert homogeneous oppositely charged polyelectrolyte solutions into condensed structured liquids via liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS). Directing these principles toward artificial, all‐proteinaceous complex coacervates enables the development of soft matter systems fully compatible with a broad range of advanced biotechnological products. Here, we employ charge‐tunable β‐lactoglobulin and lysozyme amyloid nanofibrils as building blocks toward fully proteinaceous functional materials. The functionality is dictated by engineering the composition and self‐organization of oppositely charged amyloid nanofibrils at the liquid–liquid interface.
