nf9305c8813aa: Rational design of oxide photocatalysts with intrinsically efficient bulk carrier transport remains a major challenge because carrier migration is strongly governed by the complex interplay among crystal structure, electronic structure, and chemical bonding. Here, we propose a Frontier orbital engineering strategy to regulate intrinsic carrier transport by reconstructing the Frontier orbital composition within a structurally robust oxide framework. Based on the tunnel-type Na2Ti6O13 structure, the oxide semiconductor K2Zn2Nb4O13 was designed and synthesized through the cooperative substitution of Ti4+ by Zn2+/Nb5+. Combined high-resolution PXRD and NPD refinements confirm the successful realization of the designed tunnel framework with complete Zn/Nb ordering. Orbital-resolved electronic structure and chemical bonding analyses demonstrate that the valence band maximum (VBM) and conduction band minimum (CBM) are mainly derived from Zn 3d−O 2p and Nb1 4d−O 2p antibonding orbitals, respectively. Such orbital decoupling of Frontier orbital contributing units and the continuous covalent networks along the b-axis provide favorable pathways for bulk carrier migration and establish the structural and electronic basis for the proposed Frontier orbital engineering strategy. Experimentally, Pd-loaded K2Zn2Nb4O13 exhibits enhanced photocatalytic H2 generation activity, achieving a rate of 119(3) μmol/h. This work provides Frontier orbital engineering as a design paradigm for functional materials, enabling the rational manipulation of intrinsic charge transport properties through the synergistic regulation of crystal structure, electronic structure, and chemical bonding.
n465bd8456283: Metal nanoparticle sintering in high-temperature oxidizing atmospheres remains a primary deactivation pathway for platinum-group metal catalysts on alumina supports. Here, atomic layer deposition (ALD) was used to deposit alumina on supported Pt catalysts and develop alumina-encapsulated Pt/Al2O3 catalysts that were aged at 800 °C under different atmospheres and characterized by time-resolved high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM), CO-probe diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (CO-DRIFTS), and propene combustion kinetics. Within the alumina-encapsulated system, a sub-2 nm Pt cluster population formed under all oxidizing atmospheres tested but not under inert atmosphere, and this population persisted for at least 12 h at 800 °C under propene complete combustion (PCC) conditions. Unencapsulated Pt/Al2O3 controls, by contrast, developed only a transient sub-2 nm population, detected within 1 min of aging in air at 800 °C and no longer present afterward, consistent with the rapid disappearance of small particles predicted by Ostwald ripening theory. CO-DRIFTS confirmed the presence of undercoordinated Pt surface sites in all oxidatively aged samples, with no detectable signal when the sample was aged under inert atmosphere. Propene combustion rates measured after aging for an alumina-encapsulated catalyst were approximately two and five times higher than the fresh encapsulated catalyst for catalysts aged under inert atmosphere and under oxygen and steam, respectively. DFT calculations of Pt diffusion through defective Al2O3 identified kinetically accessible diffusion pathways at 800 °C, with activation barriers as low as 0.76 eV. Furthermore, Pt surface binding was calculated to be favored in the presence of O2. These results identify oxygen-driven surface segregation, mediated by defect-assisted diffusion through the ALD overcoat, as a possible mechanism responsible for nanocluster formation in this system. The persistence of the sub-2 nm cluster population for at least 12 h at 800 °C under PCC conditions demonstrates the thermal stability of these sites within the encapsulated architecture.
ndbadc1daa7c1: Layered inorganic materials can exhibit symmetry-breaking transitions in which electronic instabilities and local structural modes are strongly intertwined. Here we compare the isovalent chalcogenides Bi2Rh3Se2 and Bi2Rh3S2 by synchrotron single-crystal X-ray diffraction and density-functional-theory calculations, and identify a static Bi2Rh4 breathing distortion as the common local motif underlying their distinct low-temperature phases. In Bi2Rh3Se2, the transition near 240 K is characterized by the loss of C-centering without a change in the conventional unit-cell volume. The resulting primitive lattice contains inequivalent Rh4 quadrilaterals formed by alternating expansion and contraction, establishing a C-centering-breaking breathing order. Although previous spectroscopic studies have reported CDW-like signatures in Bi2Rh3Se2, the calculated Fermi surfaces of the high-temperature phase do not reveal an obvious nesting vector expected for a simple nesting-driven Peierls-type CDW scenario. Instead, the Rh 4d-derived electronic states at the Fermi level are naturally sensitive to the observed Rh4 breathing distortion, indicating that the transition is best described as a breathing-order transition accompanied by electronic reconstruction. In Bi2Rh3S2, a comparable Bi2Rh4 breathing distortion appears, but its ordering pattern is switched: when described in the high-temperature-cell setting, the Bi2Rh4 units form a large−small−small sequence along the aHT-direction, accompanied by an antiphase relation between neighboring chains, producing a commensurate 3× superstructure consistent with the first-order character of the transition. Calculations based on the experimentally refined structures further reveal a reduction of the density of states near EF and an anisotropic redistribution of occupied low-energy states in the breathing-distorted phases, supporting the coupling between the Bi2Rh4 motif and electronic reconstruction. These results show that isovalent chalcogen substitution selects the in-plane ordering pattern of an intrinsic Bi2Rh4 breathing distortion, thereby switching the collective symmetry-breaking pathway and associated electronic response.
n457564aea7d6: Two-dimensional Cu nanostructures containing noncanonical face-centered cubic/hexagonal close-packed (fcc/hcp) heterophase boundaries are attractive for CO2 electroreduction but remain difficult to prepare by wet-chemical methods. Here, we report a high-temperature solution reduction route to Cu nanodisks with a thickness of 26.5 ± 2.3 nm and a diameter of 85.6 ± 3.7 nm. Transmission electron microscopy reveals abundant fcc/2H and fcc/4H interfaces on the nanodisk side surfaces, where the 2H and 4H polytypes exhibit AB and ABCB stacking, respectively. In CO2-saturated 0.1 M KHCO3, the nanodisks achieve a methane Faradaic efficiency of 60.4% at −1.25 V vs the reversible hydrogen electrode and outperform fcc Cu nanoparticle and microsheet controls tested at the same catalyst loading. Density functional theory calculations indicate that the free-energy penalty for forming the *CHO intermediate is smaller on the fcc/2H and fcc/4H models than on fcc Cu. These results support a thermodynamic contribution of heterophase interfaces to the observed methane selectivity; the calculations do not establish a reduction in kinetic activation barriers. This solution-phase route therefore provides access to phase-engineered Cu nanodisks and enables structure−property relationships relevant to CO2-to-CH4 electrocatalysis.
n0b819e8ebfc5: Earth-abundant catalysts for acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) must simultaneously achieve high geometric activity and strong resistance to oxidative dissolution. Manganese dioxide (MnO2) is a promising candidate but its dominant...
n692210636012: Stretchable solar cells could energize portable and wearable electronics, yet their efficiency and mechanical durability are measured under conditions so divergent that devices of comparable initial performance defy cross-laboratory comparison. Ye and colleagues trace this divergence to routinely overlooked factors, among them substrate properties, strain rate, and strain-induced changes in illuminated area. They introduce metrics for tolerable strain and cycle lifetime, together with a reporting checklist, establishing a shared benchmark for the field and a path to formal standardization.

n36967a5e1662: This work demonstrates an intrinsically stretchable thin-film rechargeable Na-ion battery by addressing the materials challenges and integration compatibilities across the whole battery system. The design combines biocompatible materials selection and organic Na-ion electrochemical system design, with a solvent-resistant stretchable current collector, a strain-adaptable gel polymer electrolyte, and tunable-modulus organic electrodes. It presents a promising platform for next-generation thin-film stretchable power sources for wearable and biomedical electronic devices.
nacf0cbb408c5: Liquid metal (LM) composites transform into stretchable conductors through compressive loading, but how this critical mechanical sintering process creates conductive networks has remained unclear. Here, we show that mechanical loading generates cracks that enable LM to flow, connect isolated droplets, and form persistent conductive networks. A fracture-based model captures this transition across droplet sizes and composite architectures, establishing a general framework for how fracture can reorganize embedded liquids to create function in soft materials.
nfe7396929e8b: Poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO)-based composite solid electrolytes (CSEs) suffer from poor ionic conductivity because strong Li+–ether oxygen coordination restricts Li+ transport. Herein, we develop a competitive coordination strategy by introducing a minimal amount of hexanedinitrile (HDN; 2.30 wt %) into PEO CSEs. Its flexible tetramethylene spacer allows nitrile groups to compete with PEO for Li+, forming mobile Li(HDN)x+ species while largely preserving the polymer backbone. This design accelerates local Li+ migration and promotes interfacial Li+ exchange, mitigating the trade-off between ionic conductivity and mechanical strength. The optimized CSE-HDN achieves an ionic conductivity of 4.87 × 10–4 S cm–1 (60 °C) and a tensile strength of 1.08 MPa. Li||Li symmetric cells cycle stably for 1000 h at 0.2 mA cm–2, while Li||LiFePO4 cells retain 94.8% capacity after 250 cycles at 3C. These results identify competitive Li+–nitrile coordination as a strategy for designing high-performance PEO-based CSEs.
n84308173c127: Metal oxide semiconductor gas sensors suffer from insufficient sensitivity and slow response/recovery due to inefficient charge separation and sluggish surface reaction kinetics at room temperature. Herein, we demonstrated that single-atom Cu doping enabled precise band structure engineering of W18O49, thereby enabling photoassisted room-temperature NO2 detection with high sensitivity and selectivity. Single-atom Cu induced abundant oxygen vacancies and regulated the electronic configuration, facilitating oxygen radical generation and interfacial charge transfer. Consequently, the Cu1–W18O49 sensor exhibited a high response (RNO2/Rair = 572.3) toward 10 ppm of NO2 and excellent selectivity under light. In situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy confirmed the formation of multiple nitrogen oxide species on the Cu1–W18O49 surface and revealed that the Cu doping induces a transformation of the NO3 adsorption configuration from a weak monodentate to a bidentate binding mode, highlighting the enhanced surface reactivity by Cu doping. This work provides fundamental insights into the rational design of high-performance photoactivated gas sensors.
nd7201df4b95b: Realizing high-resolution stretchable displays requires emissive materials that combine photopatternability with intrinsic stretchability. In colloidal nanocrystal films, however, the network formation needed for precise patterning often restricts molecular mobility, creating a fundamental trade-off with mechanical compliance. Here, we address this challenge using a benzophenone-based dual-crosslinker strategy that forms an elastomeric nanocrystal network. The tetrafunctional small-molecule crosslinker promotes efficient photopatterning, whereas the benzophenone-terminated polybutadiene crosslinker provides mechanical compliance. By tuning the crosslinker composition, the dual-crosslinking system enables direct optical patterning with line widths down to 2 μm and crack-free deformation up to 36% uniaxial strain. Both perovskite and InP-based nanocrystals largely retain their photoluminescence after processing, while the dual-crosslinking platform enables multicolor patterning and transfer to elastomeric substrates. QLEDs incorporating strained emissive layers maintain more than 90% of the maximum luminance of their unstretched counterparts. This dual-crosslinker design offers a general route to intrinsically stretchable, directly photopatternable colloidal nanocrystal emission layers.
ndb8de8985be1: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) are layered van der Waals semiconductors that can convert a single high-energy photon into multiple electron–hole pairs through carrier multiplication (CM). However, the factors governing CM efficiency within the TMDC family remain unclear, with studies limited to Mo- and W-based compositions. Here, we address this question by investigating HfSe2 and ReSe2, two less-explored TMDCs with markedly different electronic densities of states. Combining first-principles calculations with ultrafast optical spectroscopy, we establish the occurrence of efficient CM in both materials, with quantum yields 20–30% higher than those of previously studied multilayer TMDCs. Our analysis reveals that CM outcompetes phonon-mediated cooling. Furthermore, we observe similarly high CM efficiencies in HfSe2 and ReSe2 despite their vastly different number of possible CM pathways. This comparison reveals that the CM efficiency is mainly determined by the presence of at least a single CM decay pathway rather than the total number.
n0414d41f9479: Dense assemblies of metal nanoparticles offer a scalable route to high-index optical metamaterials, yet their collective response and loss mechanisms remain poorly understood. We synthesize quasi-spherical Ag nanoparticles with diameters ranging from 17 to 66 nm and assemble them into closely-packed monolayers. These films exhibit size-dependent refractive indices reaching a maximum of 10.3 with a low loss region emerging on the red shoulder of the resonance. We introduce a compact analytical model that quantitatively reproduces the measured optical constants and identifies the interparticle gap as the lever controlling the achievable index and loss. We compute Bergman-Milton fundamental limits, finding that our best assemblies reach two-thirds of the high-index–low-loss Pareto frontier for silver/polystyrene composites of arbitrary microstructure with the remaining samples approaching within a factor of 1.7–4. Together, experiment and theory establish silver nanoparticle assemblies as a tunable platform approaching fundamental bounds and define pathways for further performance gains.
n550cc1e0594f: Gas bubbles generated during water electrolysis alter electrolyte access, ionic conduction, and local mass transport, thereby influencing electrochemical performance. Directly resolving this process is often challenging because numerous bubbles evolve and interact simultaneously on conventional gas-evolving electrodes. Here, we establish mesoporous Pt microelectrodes as a simplified model system to examine how the nanoscale porous architecture affects H2 bubble evolution relative to nonporous Pt electrodes with the same macroscopic disk geometry at matched nominal H2 generation rates. The mesoporous Pt electrode exhibited smaller detachment diameters and shorter detachment periods during single H2 bubble evolution in H2SO4. During multiple H2 bubble evolution in HClO4, the mesoporous electrode concentrated microbubble emergence into fewer locations and developed a less crowded near interface bubble population, with a smaller current-induced resistance increment. These results show how the nanoscale porous architecture can reorganize collective bubble evolution and thereby modify the associated ohmic penalty during electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution.
n20ee2a95b96a: Nanoparticle-on-mirror (NPoM) cavities confine light within molecular gaps, but conventional drop casting does not register cavities at predefined coordinates. We integrate electron-beam lithography, face-selective DNA origami placement, and DNA-mediated gold-nanosphere docking to position molecularly programmable NPoMs on flat gold mirrors. Across six patches containing 2538 sites in total, the estimated mean single-particle occupation was approximately 84.7%. Dark-field spectra of cavities programmed with cyanine 5 (Cy5) show a split response centered near the Cy5 transition. Comparison with bare-cavity sweeps of facet width, gap thickness, and spacer index supports a molecularly anchored, Rabi-like interpretation of this response within a damped coupled-oscillator model. Photoluminescence controls reveal substantial gold luminescence, so dark-field scattering is used as the primary coupling observable. The platform therefore combines deterministic cavity registration with sequence-programmable molecular optical functionality.
n55c9f680d28a: Pancreatic β-cell ferroptosis, driven by oxidative stress and impaired glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) activity, has emerged as an important contributor to the progression of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). However, persistent reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and insufficient selenocysteine (Sec) availability limit GPX4-dependent antioxidant defense, making effective ferroptosis intervention challenging. Here, we engineered a ROS-responsive Sec-loaded copper-based single-atom nanozyme (Se@CuSAzyme) that combines catalytic ROS scavenging with Sec supplementation. Benefiting from its intrinsic superoxide dismutase- and catalase-like activities, Se@CuSAzyme efficiently eliminated excessive ROS, while oxidative stress-triggered Sec release enhanced GPX4 expression. As a result, Se@CuSAzyme markedly suppressed high glucose and erastin-induced ferroptosis, reduced lipid peroxidation, and preserved mitochondrial integrity in pancreatic β-cells. In high-fat diet/streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice, Se@CuSAzyme demonstrated therapeutic efficacy comparable to that of metformin in ameliorating hyperglycemia, alleviating insulin resistance, and increasing energy expenditure. Importantly, Se@CuSAzyme outperformed metformin in protecting against hepatic steatosis and glycolipid metabolic dysfunction.
n3518e93e2fe6: Optical chirality has been extensively explored in chiral molecules, helical structures, and metasurfaces with bound states in the continuum. Attempts to attain chirality have mainly relied on human intuition and ideas. Here, we show various types of single-layer silicon-nanostructured metasurfaces exhibiting prominent circular dichroism (CD) containing perfect, broadband, and opposite CD responses at short near-infrared wavelengths. The designs were obtained based on a generative AI-assisted structural search for chiral metasurfaces, enabling a series of nonempirical structural searches beyond the boundary of human knowledge and experience. The physical mechanisms yielding the outstanding CD responses are elucidated from detailed insights into subwavelength electromagnetic dynamics in the single-layer metasurfaces. Furthermore, we experimentally demonstrate several metasurfaces. This type of single-layer thin CD metasurface serves as a key element in the development of compact optical-wave-manipulating devices at telecommunication bands.
nfbea2b2ee9ff: Cisplatin (CDDP) requires a rate-limiting intracellular aquation to generate aquated cisplatin (aqCDDP) for DNA binding and exertion of oncostatic effects. On this basis, three isomeric bile salt-aqCDDP nanocomplexes (12α-SDC@CDDP, 7α-SCDC@CDDP, and 7β-SUDC@CDDP) were constructed to directly deliver aqCDDP. Although 7β-SUDC@CDDP exhibited the optimal pharmacokinetics, poor cellular uptake resulted in limited tumor accumulation and insufficient antitumor activity. For 7α-SCDC@CDDP, the nonspecific distribution in the liver and lung resulted in suboptimal antitumor activity. Notably, 12α-SDC@CDDP demonstrated 3-fold higher tumor accumulation than CDDP solution and the best antitumor activity owing to its highest cellular uptake. These results revealed that the stereochemical configuration of the hydroxyl group on bile salts regulated the trade-off between systemic circulation and cellular internalization, with 12α-hydroxylation favoring uptake and 7β-hydroxylation favoring circulation. These findings provided guiding implications for future bile salt–platinum nanomedicine design, particularly through stereochemical regulation to improve therapeutic performance.
n50981ca61ad7: Lithium–sulfur batteries have emerged as a promising candidate for next-generation energy storage systems due to high theoretical energy density and low cost. However, the practical application is severely hindered by issues such as the polysulfide shuttle effect, sluggish ion transport, and lithium dendrite growth. Here, we proposed a synergistic strategy based on nanoconfinement polymerization and self-healing dynamic cross-linking to successfully fabricate a self-healing composite solid electrolyte, composed of PVDF-HFP, graphene oxide, UiO-66, linear polydopamine chains, and a boronic ester cross-linked network. The electrolyte demonstrates high ionic conductivity (1.7 × 10–4 S cm–1), good puncture resistance (9.7 N), high elongation at break (335%), and superior capacity retention (a capacity decay rate of 0.0276% per cycle over 500 cycles). Even under a high sulfur loading of 4 mg cm–2, the capacity retention remained as high as 94.8%, which exceeds previously reported electrolytes. This strategy offers a new pathway to designing advanced solid electrolytes for high-energy batteries.
n69218a252dae: Controlling phase evolution and composition homogeneity are challenging for chalcopyrites. Ma, Wu, Liu, Yan et al. use acetate anions to build complex networks in precursor solution, achieving single-phase crystallization and an 18.53% efficient Cu(In,Ga)Se2 solar cell.
n10a60b686412: Bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells are promising for high area-normalized power output, but factors governing the photothermal stability of perovskite absorbers remains unclear. Xu et al. identify lattice compliance as a descriptor when screening stable perovskites.
nef61abb22bef: Sulfur-based redox flow batteries promise low-cost, long-duration energy storage using abundant active materials, but commercial success depends on much more than low-cost materials. Yi-Chun Lu and her team explore how deployment reshapes research priorities and reveals the scientific and engineering bottlenecks that determine technology translation.
nb5b35a1a035c: The electron-beam-assisted subtraction method enables the controllable fabrication of free-standing metal oxide monolayers, along with lateral heterostructures and twisted bilayers, expanding the material space of 2D quantum systems.
nd2fa4369b0d5: Photonic metasurfaces patterned in anisotropic ReS2 create robust, spectrally scalable directional photonic flatbands, enabling the topological control of polarization-resolved exciton–polaritons and enhanced light–matter coupling.
n5bc0595f6a2c: Layered metal oxyhalides can be selectively dehalogenated inside a scanning transmission electron microscope, yielding free-standing monolayer oxide sheets and coupling synthesis with atomic-resolution observation.
n3923abf06e24: Porous liquids combine permanent porosity with fluidity, extending the design of porous materials beyond conventional solid frameworks. This Perspective outlines universal design principles, emerging synthetic strategies and theory-guided methodologies that enable rational control of permanent porosity, fluidity and functionality, accelerating the predictive development of next-generation porous liquids.
n76f9dd444ce1: By decoupling ceramic-film densification from high-temperature sintering, molten-salt-mediated liquid-phase growth enables a dense, compositionally uniform proton-conducting thin film to form at 800 °C, despite its melting point exceeding 2,700 °C. This strategy opens opportunities for low-temperature ceramic fabrication and on-demand materials design.
n6811a7cf5f78: While product-induced inhibition is widely recognized in heterogeneous catalysis, the joint influence of co-generated products on time-dependent catalytic deactivation remains underexplored. Herein, uniform colloidal Pt nanoparticles were deposited on anatase TiO2 supports selectively exposing (101) or (001) facets to fabricate two facet-controlled model Pt/TiO2 catalysts. We uncovered the intrinsic deactivation mechanism for low-temperature lean propylene combustion via stability tests, alternating feed kinetics, in situ DRIFTS, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Time-on-stream reaction tests recorded persistent activity decay for both catalysts, with far more serious decay observed on Pt/TiO2(101). Multiple characterization results excluded Pt sintering/encapsulation, C3H6/O2 poisoning, and partial Pt oxidation as dominant degradation factors. Instead, CO2 adsorption and subsequent carbonate accumulation on TiO2 surfaces were identified as the primary deactivation sources, which cut off supplementary oxygen delivery at metal–support interfaces. DFT adsorption energy data proved that H2O possessed a stronger surface affinity than CO2 on both facet types, and in situ generated H2O competed for adsorption sites to curb carbonate accumulation. Apart from this competitive effect, reaction-derived H2O alleviated excessive coverage of Pt sites by C3H6 and facilitated the adsorption and activation of gas-phase O2. Thanks to the relatively high water-binding capacity of TiO2(001), the corresponding Pt/TiO2(001) catalyst maintained abundant interfacial water during operation and exhibited much milder carbonate-triggered decay. These findings clarified the competitive co-adsorption interplay between CO2 and H2O across Pt–TiO2 interfaces and offered general kinetic guidance for developing durable catalysts toward industrial hydrocarbon lean combustion.
n4e7645774dbe: The electrochemical urea oxidation reaction (UOR) has emerged as an attractive anodic reaction for various energy conversion systems. Recently, increasing attention has been directed toward controlling UOR selectivity on Ni-based electrocatalysts following the recognition that the UOR can produce over-oxidized products. However, existing studies have focused predominantly on catalyst design to regulate surface-bound intermediates, whereas whether electrolyte-mediated noncovalent interactions can selectively control competing UOR pathways remains poorly understood. Here, we show that rational electrolyte engineering using alkali-metal cations selectively regulates the UOR pathway by modulating the interfacial hydrogen-bonding network. Electrochemical rate deconvolution and product analysis reveal that weakly hydrated cations selectively accelerate the direct oxidation pathway, promoting the formation of the over-oxidized NO2– and NCO– products, while leaving the indirect pathway essentially unaffected. In situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) measurements, together with molecular dynamics simulations of cation hydration dynamics, indicate that weakly hydrated cations create a more dynamic interfacial water environment with faster water exchange, thereby facilitating interfacial OH–-mediated successive dehydrogenation during direct urea oxidation. Leveraging this mechanistic understanding, the electrolyte-engineering strategy was applied to a cascade urea-to-ammonia conversion system, achieving a urea-to-ammonia conversion efficiency of 77.5% and approximately threefold higher ammonia productivity in CsOH than in LiOH. These findings establish electrolyte engineering as a complementary strategy to catalyst design and highlight noncovalent electrolyte–electrode interactions as an effective handle for controlling reaction pathways and product selectivity in an integrated UOR-based nitrogen conversion system.
n023e8bde5912: Nitrogen-rich azo-tetrazole compounds are essential structural scaffolds for energetic materials, dyes, and agrochemicals, owing to their favorable energetic and physicochemical properties. Potassium 5,5′-azotetrazolate (PZT), as a representative and efficient nitrogen-rich azo-tetrazole material, is conventionally synthesized via thermochemical oxidative coupling, which suffers from safety hazards and environmental pollution. Electrochemical synthesis offers a compelling alternative, but the severe competitive oxygen evolution reaction (OER) impedes achieving highly-efficient N–N coupling activity and Faradaic efficiency (FE). Herein, a core–shell CF@CuO@Ni/Ni(OH)2 electrode is fabricated through controlled H+-mediated electrodeposition. The CF@CuO core provides a three-dimensional (3D) conductive scaffold and suppresses the competing OER, while the Ni0/Ni(OH)2 shell undergoes electrochemical reconstruction into coexisting NiO/NiOOH working phases. The catalyst reaches 10 mA·cm–2 at 1.16 V vs RHE and maintains a Faradaic efficiency above 94% over a broad potential range of 1.2–1.6 V. Combined electrochemical, spectroscopic, kinetic, and computational analyses prove that surface-adsorbed *OH initiates 5-AT dehydrogenative coupling via a PCET pathway on the reconstructed NiO/NiOOH surface. NiO triggers synergistic *OH/5-AT adsorption, while NiOOH facilitates dehydrogenation. In a continuous-flow AEM electrolyzer, the system operates at 500 mA cm–2 over 300 h while sustaining PZT production (purity ≥99%) and H2 evolution. Extension to DAT and DAF further demonstrates the transferability of the catalyst toward related amino-functionalized N-heterocycles undergoing oxidative N–N coupling. This work establishes that reconstructed NiO/NiOOH dual sites, supported on an OER-suppressing CuO scaffold, enable selective and energy-efficient N–N oxidative coupling of amino heterocycles.
nbdaa452eaad5: Selective ethanol dehydrogenation is a promising route for acetaldehyde production; however, achieving stable copper catalysts on inert supports with a well-balanced Cu+/Cu0 ratio remains challenging. Herein, we report a urea-assisted strategy to simultaneously stabilize copper species and regulate the Cu+/Cu0 balance on a silica support. The gradual release of ammonia promotes the formation of interfacial Cu–O–Si linkages and basic copper nitrate species, which serve as precursors for Cu+ and Cu0, respectively. The resulting catalyst exhibits highly dispersed copper species with a balanced Cu+/Cu0 distribution, delivering high activity, >95% acetaldehyde selectivity, and stable performance in ethanol dehydrogenation. Mechanistic studies reveal that Cu+ sites facilitate ethanol activation, while Cu0 sites promote C–H bond cleavage. However, excessive Cu+ species lead to the formation of strongly adsorbed enolic intermediates, which trigger C–C coupling and byproduct formation. This work highlights the importance of Cu+/Cu0 synergy and provides a general strategy for designing stable and selective copper-based catalysts on inert supports.
n7eff34347f13: Aqueous redox flow batteries (ARFBs) comprising earth-abundant charge carriers could cheaply store grid-scale renewable electricity, but most lab-scale systems have a low open-circuit potential (OCP) that inflates system cost. We report a non-hybrid aqueous flow cell with an OCP of 2.2 V, among the highest reported for this class, pairing an alkaline chromium-1,3-propylenediaminetetraacetate negolyte with an acidic bromide posolyte. The two electrolytes maintain an approximately seven-unit pH gradient across a single cation-exchange membrane, without external oxygen or a bipolar-membrane recovery sub-cell: operando pH measurements and a zero-dimensional model show that the difference is sustained passively by balancing slow proton crossover against hydrogen evolution and positive-side acid generation. The cell cycles for 240 h with a Coulombic efficiency of up to 99.5%; tuning the posolyte additive, electrode, and membrane raises the peak power density to 534 mW cm–2 at 43 °C.
ncf6b42c3c595: Aqueous polysulfide redox flow batteries (RFBs) are promising for large-scale energy storage owing to their low cost and high safety. However, stable operation at high current density remains challenging for polysulfide RFBs (typically cycling below 40 mA cm–2), with the degradation mechanisms remaining poorly understood. Here, we identify current density as a critical factor governing the cycle life and elucidate sulfur deposition-induced degradation. Increasing current density simultaneously accelerates polysulfide crossover and promotes the formation of compact sulfur deposits, which block ion-transport pathways and lead to rapid cell failure. Based on this mechanistic understanding, a surfactant additive was employed to regulate sulfur nucleation and growth, extending the cycle life of polysulfide/ferrocyanide RFBs from 30 cycles to over 500 cycles at 60 mA cm–2. This work elucidates current density and sulfur morphology as critical factors governing polysulfide RFB degradation and provides design principles for durable, high-rate polysulfide-based RFBs.
n4fcf93d66726: While high-power lithium-ion capacitors (LICs) with high energy density emerge as promising pulse-/peak-power solutions for AI data centers, their long-term viability remains severely hindered by the degradation of the activated carbon (AC) positive electrode. To evaluate this aging behavior, we propose a 24-h high-voltage cycling (HVC) protocol integrated with operando Raman spectroscopy, demonstrating that the turning point in the D1 band can serve as a sensitive indicator of corrosion severity. During the early-stage HVC aging, cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) formation and gas evolution passivate defect-related Raman signals, narrowing the D1 band. As aging proceeds, carbon corrosion becomes dominant and broadens the D1 band. By validating this approach across various ACs, we establish a direct correlation between an earlier structural turning point and accelerated capacity decay, thereby uncovering carbon aging mechanisms and offering an unprecedented, rapid diagnostic technique for capacitor-type materials.
nee6d47ab7b6a: Achieving complete reversibility in martensite–austenite phase transitions is challenging due to structural degradation during thermal cycling, yet the atomistic pathways driving this degradation remain unresolved. Using in situ atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy on a Ni2MnGa shape-memory alloy, we reveal that although structural modulation forms through phonon softening to relieve mismatch strain between martensite and austenite, it significantly compromises reversibility. While the global lattice shear in nonmodulated martensite is reversible, the localized atomic shuffles in the modulated structure do not reverse collectively. Instead, they follow locally divergent pathways that create a kinetically arrested austenite state. Upon cooling, this arrested state triggers irregular atomic shuffling and residual defects that produce thermal hysteresis and functional fatigue. Linking this degradation to the multidirectional energy landscape of atomic shuffling provides a framework for understanding kinetic trapping and reversibility in complex materials.
nb1946f873628: Protein functions are closely linked to their dynamic behaviors, particularly involving low-abundance transient states. Quantifying these interconversions remains experimentally challenging, especially for proteins containing intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs). In this study, we utilize low-dose electron microscopy using graphene liquid cells to image and quantify interconversions between protein conformational states under optimized electron beam conditions and confinement effects. Applied to four proteins in solution: CRISPR-associated protein (Cas9), DNA binding protein (GapR), restriction enzyme (EcoRI), and an RNA binding protein with IDRs (FUS), we visualized low-abundance transient structures distinct from crystalline forms and elucidated transition pathways which are validated by cryo-electron microscopy, revealing differences in their energy landscapes through single-molecule imaging. We analyzed domain-scale rearrangements at ∼1–2 nm effective conformational resolution, cross-validated against independent computational and experimental methods. Shifts in state equilibria and conformational adaptations were observed when proteins are mutated or during biomolecular interactions, such as target searching, binding, and cleavage with nucleic acids. Notably, changes in the energy landscape were observed when proteins with IDRs and RNA were within close proximity but not in apparent contact, suggesting that conformational redistribution may precede complete binding. This study shows how to characterize protein conformations and their time-dependent changes using instrumentation that is widely available at research universities but not yet used for these purposes.
n6e3e634c6646: Aqueous ammonium-ion (NH4 +) batteries (AAIBs) have recently emerged as promising alternatives for next-generation energy storage, owing to the unique hydrogen-bond-assisted diffusion of NH4 + ions within the host lattice framework. However, research on electrode materials remains limited, and a considerable gap persists between laboratory scale and practical applications due to the low mass loadings (1–5 mg cm−2) of conventional electrodes. This work introduces an ultrahigh mass-loading integrated 3D-printed porous conductive electrode of functional metal tellurides, Bi2-xSbxTe3 (0 ≤ x ≤ 1.5) as an efficient anode for AAIBs. To address the limited ion diffusion associated with ultrahigh mass-loading electrodes, Bi2-xSbxTe3 is integrated with a 3D-printed porous titanium alloy (Ti6Al4V) substrate fabricated via the Selective Laser Melting (SLM) technique. Such an interconnected porous framework provides efficient mass-transport pathways even at very high mass-loading levels. The designed 3D-printed Bi2Te3 anode with a mass loading of 40 mg cm−2 achieves an impressive areal capacity of 9 mAh cm−2 at 2 mA cm−2, while still retaining an exceptional specific capacity of 224 mAh g−1. To improve the cyclic stability, smaller Sb3+ ions are incorporated into the Bi2Te3 lattice to strengthen the M─Te (M═Bi/Sb) bonds, which consequently mitigates volume fluctuations during cycling. Overall, this study demonstrates the potential of 3D-printed Bi2-xSbxTe3 anodes for advancing AAIB technology.
n3b85c6337296: Multifunctional additives addressing zinc anode interfac ial instability face inherent trade-offs among surface adsorption, solvation control, and pH buffering. Inspired by the “Goldilocks effect” of the clinical antihypertensive drug lisinopril (LNPL), we propose a biomimetic amphiphilic electrolyte additive strategy to achieve interfacial microenvironment homeostasis. Systematic investigations reveal that long-term zinc stability is governed by a homeostatic balance among multiple competing interfacial regulatory processes, rather than maximizing each individual function independently. At the homeostatic equilibrium achieved with 1 mM, LNPL preferentially adsorbs on the zinc surface to suppress contact with H2O and SO4 2−, adaptively buffers local pH fluctuations through reversible proton exchange, and simultaneously modulates the Zn2+ solvation environment by reducing coordinated water. Furthermore, LNPL induces a ZnO/ZnS/organic-rich hybrid SEI that suppresses side reactions, homogenizes Zn2+ flux, and inhibits dendrite growth. Consequently, the Zn||Zn cell exhibits stable cycling for over 6600 h, and the Zn||Cu cell achieves an average coulombic efficiency of 99.85% over 3000 cycles. Meanwhile, the Zn||I2 full cell achieves over 20 000 cycles with 98.3% capacity retention, while the pouch cell delivers 1.2 Ah with 84.6% retention after 200 cycles. This work establishes a Goldilocks-inspired design principle for multifunctional electrolyte additives in aqueous metal batteries.
n79c672f29d90: PtPd‐based high‐entropy alloys (HEAs) with sub‐nano‐thick ribbon morphology are a class of promising catalysts for electrochemical reactions; however, a lack of a general synthetic method that allows extensive compositional modulation for probing untold catalytic powers. Herein, we report a universal strategy for constructing PtPd‐based sub‐nanoribbons (SNRs) with tunable alloy elements for boosting oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). In this synthetic method, a ligand collection is organized to balance the large differences in redox potentials of multiple metal precursors and enforce ribbon‐like anisotropic growth. By diversifying composition, SNRs can be tuned from low‐entropy alloys to HEAs. For acidic ORR, the catalytic performance of SNRs improves as entropy increases, wherein the high‐entropy PtPdNiFeGa SNRs exhibit optimal catalytic activity and superior stability. Our theoretical investigations suggest that more bonding states are formed in the HEAs, which is conducive to creating new active sites with greater electron accumulation near the Fermi level for low‐barrier electron transfer, besides resulting in a denser crystal structure with robust catalytic stability. When equipped in the membrane electrode assembly, the PtPdNiFeGa SNRs deliver a remarkable mass activity (MA = 0.79 A/mgPt at 0.9 V) and stability (MA retention = 82% after 30 000 cycles), outperforming most of the reported PtPd‐based catalysts.
na1ed62e381bb: Integrated energy‐storage sensing devices promote greatly the miniaturization and integration of wearable electronic devices. However, they still face long‐lasting challenges of tailored semi‐integrated configuration or highly‐coupled sensing and energy storage functions. Herein, an unprecedented all‐in‐one sensing supercapacitor (ASS) is proposed for independent and synchronous strain sensing and self‐powering. The ASS features a shared configuration, endows it with several key features, including reversible changes of ion‐transport paths and resistance in porous electrolyte, robust electron transport in the dense electrode, and stable interface resistance in the chain‐entangled interfaces. These guarantee reliable sensing and charge‐discharge processes under compression. Consequently, the ASS exhibits satisfactory electrochemical performance, including low interface‐resistance, high areal‐capacitance (37.9 mF cm−2), and good stability (98.8% capacitance retention after 5000 cycles), which can be well maintained under wide compressive strains of 0%∼80% and 5000 cyclic compression‐release. Furthermore, good sensing characteristics are also achieved with wide detection ranges up to 80% compressive strain and superior durability (>7000 cycles). The ASS also shows minimal mutual interference in synchronous sensing‐powering mode over harsh conditions, highlighting its great multi‐scenario applications. These findings open up a new perspective for highly efficient all‐in‐one energy‐storage sensing devices toward practical wearable applications.
n654f820efae6: Water electrolysis offers a scalable route to green hydrogen, but its anodic half‐reaction is still constrained by the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), a sluggish four‐electron process that consumes voltage while yielding low‐value O2. Anodic high‐value conversion (AHVC) replaces this value‐losing step with product‐forming oxidation, enabling hydrogen evolution to be coupled with upgrading of oxygenated organics, nitrogen‐containing molecules, pollutants, and polymer or waste‐derived streams. Yet the promise of AHVC is not established by lower oxidation potential alone. Useful co‐production requires selective bond transformation, suppression of overoxidation and OER re‐entry, controlled intermediate fate, limited crossover, and recoverable product streams at relevant current densities. This Review develops a value‐retention framework for AHVC. We discuss the thermodynamic and kinetic origins of alternative anodic reactions, compare major substrate families and their product windows, and examine how working phases, interfacial adsorption, reactive oxygen species, and local microenvironments steer molecular pathways. Device translation is then considered through full‐cell metrics, membrane transport, product recovery, durability, and techno‐economic boundaries. By connecting molecular selectivity with electrolyzer operation, AHVC is framed as a route to energy‐saving hydrogen and value‐added chemical co‐production, rather than a simple OER substitute.
n7c2e16ca7a94: Hydrogel electrolytes are promising candidates for flexible energy storage, yet most rely on petroleum-derived polymers, raising significant sustainability and environmental concerns. Herein, we report a bio-based, biodegradable, and closed-loop recyclable hyaluronic acid (HA)/sodium alginate (SA) hydrogel electrolyte with zinc sulfate (denoted as ZHS) for zinc-iodine batteries. Leveraging abundant hydrophilic groups (─OH, ─CONH─, and ─COOH) in these natural polysaccharides, ZHS simultaneously addresses the environmental burden of synthetic gels and the electrochemical challenges of Zn-I2 batteries. Competitive hydrogen bonding between HA/SA and H2O molecules, coupled with dynamic water redistribution along polymer chains, yields a uniform and robust dual-network architecture. This network provides homogeneous pathways for rapid Zn2+ transport and suppresses dendrite nucleation, while abundant polar adsorption sites immobilize polyiodides (I3 − and I5 −) through ion-dipole interactions, alleviating shuttle effects. Consequently, Zn||Zn symmetric cells cycle stably for over 2,600 h, and Zn||I2 full cells achieve remarkable durability exceeding 35,000 cycles. Notably, the ZHS hydrogel demonstrates excellent biocompatibility and can be readily biodegraded under ambient conditions. Furthermore, cycled ZHS can be regenerated through simple aqueous dissolution and re-casting, supporting stable operation for an additional 21,000 cycles. This work pioneers a sustainable pathway toward environmentally benign, high-performance gel electrolytes for zinc-iodine batteries.
na4fae5f99a40: Electrolyte design is fundamentally constrained by the trade‐off between high solvent polarity and weak Li+ solvation, as polar solvents typically bind Li+ strongly. Here, we establish a steric–electronic modulation strategy that decouples solvent polarity from Li+ coordination, enabling a generalizable pseudo‐weak solvation electrolyte design paradigm. Based on this principle, a steric hindrance–mediated electrolyte is developed combining 2,2,2‐trifluoro‐N, N‐dimethylethylamide (DMTFA) and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) with dual lithium salts. Despite its strong polarity, DMTFA exhibits weak Li+ coordination due to the combined steric hindrance and electron‐withdrawing effects of the ‐CF3 group, enabling anion‐ dominated solvation structures. This coordination chemistry lowers Li+ desolvation barriers and drives the preferential adsorption of a B‐ and P‐rich interphase layer at the cathode surface, thereby protecting the cathode from HF corrosion. The resulting electrolyte achieves high ionic conductivity, intrinsic flame retardancy, and an electrochemical stability window exceeding 5.0 V. Cells employing LiNi0.91Co0.06Mn0.03O2 cathodes demonstrate a capacity retention of over 90.0% after 100 cycles at 1 C rate and 4.8 V charge cut‐off. The electrolyte enables approximately 1.6 Ah pouch cells to retain 84.97% capacity after 1800 cycles at 4.6 V.
n013f4e4289b0: Lithium Batteries In article number e71380, Stefano Passerini, Shan Fang, and co‐workers established a steric‐electronic synergistic regulation strategy that decouples solvent polarity from Li+ coordination strength. Bulky ‐CF3 groups create a “pseudo‐weak solvation” environment in polar solvents, breaking the polarity‐coordination paradigm without sacrificing salt solubility. This enables stable high‐voltage cycling. The work offers a universal framework for advanced high‐energy lithium battery electrolytes.
n72caa931b53f: The reliance on high stack pressure in lithium metal batteries (LMBs) conflicts with the requirements of lightweight design and low‐pressure operating environments, motivating the development of pressure‐independent battery designs. Here, a chemical bonding interfacial prototype is proposed to substitute the physical contact interface, thereby liberating LMBs from high stacking pressures. This chemical bonding interface is constructed via strong interactions between the carbonyl groups of poly(ε‐caprolactone) segments and Li metal, manifesting as Li─O bonding interfaces. Benefiting from Li─O bonding, the PPE electrolyte exhibits a high adhesion energy of 22.44 J m−2 and a high lap shear strength of 0.31 MPa, sustaining intimate electrode–electrolyte contact without external stack pressure. In addition, the Li─O bonding interface significantly reduces the thickness of the electric double layer, achieving a 120% increase in capacitance (0.20 µF cm−2), thus promoting efficient transport (tLi+ = 0.7) and uniform deposition of Li+. As a result, the Li||Cu half‐cell equipped with PPE electrolyte achieves a superior coulombic efficiency of 99.78%. A pouch cell equipped with PPE electrolyte and NCM cathode demonstrates high capacity retention of 90.12% after 40 cycles at −0.1 MPa (relative to standard atmospheric pressure). This discovery offers novel insights into material and structural design for pressure‐insensitive batteries intended for high‐altitude aerospace applications.
n691410a29622: Understanding charge generation in organic photovoltaics remains a central challenge despite recent efficiency gains. Here, competing charge separation pathways in donor:acceptor blends are identified by directly probing photoinduced spin states using transient electron spin resonance (ESR) spectroscopy, enabling distinction between charge‐transfer states and separated charges. The results reveal that, across fullerene and non‐fullerene acceptor blends, charge generation proceeds via two pathways: a fast pathway forming separated charges on timescales faster than spin mixing, and a slower pathway mediated by spin‐polarized interfacial charge‐transfer (CT) states. Modeling of the time‐dependent evolution of spin polarization across blends and temperatures quantifies the relative contributions of these charge separation pathways and resolves subsequent charge dynamics, governed by a balance of dissociation, re‐encounter, and spin‐selective recombination via CT states. Analysis of CT‐state ESR spectra provides a link between charge separation dynamics and morphology by identifying interfacial donor:acceptor geometries associated with the slower charge separation pathway. The results show that higher‐performing blends, particularly PM6:Y6, are characterized by dominance of the faster charge separation pathway and dynamic interconversion between CT states and separated charges. These findings emphasize the importance of balancing fast charge separation with efficient re‐dissociation of CT states for achieving high performance in organic photovoltaic materials.
n4b6071553989: Solid‐state lithium‐metal batteries leveraging solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) represent a promising technological pathway. Among these, polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF)‐based SPEs are particularly noteworthy, yet they face a fundamental dilemma: electrode/electrolyte interfacial degradation from solvent‐dominated Li+ coordination versus constrained Li+ transport under solvent‐deficient conditions. To resolve this paradox, a 3D porous few‐layered MoS2 was synthesized and employed as the filler in PVDF‐based SPEs. The fillers concurrently weaken Li+ coordination with both FSI− and solvent through targeted dipole interactions, thereby enhancing Li+ migration rate and inducing structural reorganization to anion‐dominated Li+ solvation. The optimized PVDF‐based electrolyte demonstrates record‐breaking ionic conductivity (1.13 mS cm−1), Li+ transference number (0.68), and exceptional compatibility with lithium metal anodes under solvent‐lean conditions. The LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2||Li cell demonstrates exceptional cycling stability, achieving a record‐high capacity retention of 90.5% after 1500 cycles at 2 C. Furthermore, practical applicability is confirmed through a 54 mAh pouch cell configuration. The ultra‐stable interfacial characteristics establish new performance benchmarks, demonstrating a viable pathway toward practical solid‐state batteries with minimal solvent dependence.
n8010edcb169a: Anode‐free lithium metal batteries (AFLMBs) maximize energy density by eliminating anode host materials, but their lifetime is governed by Li deposition on the current collector (CC)—a heterogeneous nucleation and growth process. Current research mainly focuses on electrolyte or artificial interphase engineering, whereas how the CC's physical structure dictates initial deposition behavior remains unclear. Here, we show that the microstructure of Cu foils induces two distinct Li deposition modes: localized nucleation‐selective growth (LS) and distributed nucleation‐competitive coalescence (DCC). Using HLCu and nmCu as model interfaces, we elucidate the evolution pathways of these modes. By integrating AFM, iSCAT, ToF‐SIMS and operando EIS‐DRT, we reveal mode‐specific differences in nucleation sites, interfacial kinetics, and the coupling between morphology, mechanical response, and side reactions. The LS mode generates loose, non‐uniform Li deposits with strong gas evolution, whereas the DCC mode enables dense, continuous, and kinetically stable Li layers. This work demonstrates that the CC is not a passive substrate but a critical component that determines the deposition mode and performance degradation. Optimizing the physical structure of the CC interface offers a key strategy—beyond electrolyte and interphase design—for long‐life AFLMBs.
nbdca2ec9cadf: Symmetry perturbation of planar FeN4 moieties in Fe─N─C single-atom catalysts holds great promise for elevating oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) performance, yet atomically precise coordination engineering of thermodynamically stable configurations with efficient O2 mass-transport integration remains challenging. Herein, a nitrogen-mediated thermal activation strategy is proposed to construct a sublayer-engineered Fe-N5 single-atom catalyst, termed FeN5-ANDCL, featuring an axially N-bridged dual-carbon-layer architecture integrated into a hollow carbon framework. The elaborately engineered FeN5-ANDCL enables cross-scale structural orchestration, wherein the atomic-scale axial N-bridged sublayer steers cross-layer charge transfer and triggers Fe dz 2 -O 2p orbitals rehybridization, thereby elevating electron occupancy of antibonding states to weaken *OH adsorption, while the hollow carbon framework ameliorates O2 diffusion resistance and streamlines transport pathways to achieve efficient mass-transport. The unique configuration endows FeN5-ANDCL with exceptional ORR activity, attaining a high half-wave potential of 0.927 V vs. RHE in alkaline media. When deployed in zinc-air batteries, it delivers a peak power density of 307.3 mW cm−2 and remarkable cycling stability sustained for 1400 h. Collectively, this work establishes sublayer engineering for precise coordination regulation of single-atom catalysts and demonstrates a cross-scale orchestration principle that couples local electronic-structure optimization with macroscopic transport regulation for efficient electrocatalysis.
n4a76665d7437: Hard carbon (HC) is the leading anode candidate for sodium‐ion batteries, but its practical optimization remains constrained by an unresolved question: which structural motifs actually store Na+ at low potential? Early voltage‐profile assignments separated sloping capacity from plateau capacity and attributed them to adsorption, intercalation, or pore filling. However, recent evidence indicates that these assignments are often sample‐dependent and may overinterpret individual characterization signatures. This Review re‐examines HC anodes from the perspective of site‐resolved Na storage. We first compare the evolution of sodium‐storage models and clarify what each model explains, where it fails, and why apparently contradictory conclusions have emerged. We then focus on the low‐voltage plateau, discussing monolayer Na accumulation, quasi‐metallic Na cluster formation, closed‐pore filling, and the remaining pore‐volume paradox. Particular attention is given to the strengths and limitations of WAXS/XRD, SAXS, XPS, Raman, NMR, titration, and theoretical simulations for assigning Na storage states. Finally, we connect mechanistic understanding to active‐site design, including defects, heteroatoms, pores, metal‐assisted motifs, and surface functional groups, emphasizing which design rules are established and which remain speculative. HC design must move beyond qualitative structure‐performance correlations toward quantitative active‐site identification, closed‐pore metrology, and full‐cell‐relevant optimization of plateau capacity, initial Coulombic efficiency, and scalability.
n3f134c5e41d9: Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) that directly convert natural gas into electricity are promising high‐efficiency energy‐conversion devices, yet conventional Ni‐based anodes suffer from severe carbon deposition and sulfur poisoning, leading to rapid electrode deactivation. Although binary alloying effectively regulates surface reaction pathways and improves anode stability, its development largely relies on experience‐driven trial‐and‐error screening. Here, we propose a rational screening framework that integrates microkinetic analysis with deep neural networks to identify the Ni‐Ga alloy from a vast binary alloy chemical space. Density functional theory confirms that such a Ni‐Ga alloy combines efficient methane activation with intrinsic resistance to carbon deposition. Guided by these predictions, we further construct a nanocomposite electrode with Gd0.1Ce0.9O1.95 (GDC)‐encapsulated Ni‐Ga alloys (NiGa‐GDC). Benefiting from alloy‐induced electronic structure modulation and a nanocomposite electrode architecture, the NiGa‐GDC nanocomposite anode exhibits exceptional electrochemical performance and coking resistance. In nearly dry methane fuel (3% H2O), a corresponding electrolyte‐supported single cell achieves both high peak power density and durable operation, far outperforming the counterpart Ni‐GDC nanocomposite anode. Moreover, the NiGa‐GDC anode demonstrates remarkable resistance to sulfur poisoning. This study provides a new strategy for developing highly active and durable nickel‐based nanocomposite anodes for the direct utilization of natural gas.
n42e2280be5de: Aqueous zinc‐iodine batteries (ZIBs) are promising for grid‐scale energy storage owing to their intrinsic safety and high theoretical capacity. However, their development is hindered by the coupled degradation at both electrodes: uncontrollable zinc dendrites growth at the Zn anode and polyiodide shuttling at the iodine cathode. Herein, we develop a decoupled interface engineering strategy based on a low‐cost organic molecule, 2,5‐di‐tert‐butylhydroquinone (DBHQ), which exhibits potential‐coordinated functionality. At the anode side during charging, the DBHQ layer creates a hydrophobic yet zincophilic interface to guide uniform Zn deposition and suppress hydrogen evolution, enabling a Zn//Zn cell to stably cycle for 6500 h at 1 mAh cm−2. During discharging at the cathode side, such a layer acts as an efficient polyiodide trapper via strong physical adsorption. The synergistic effect in the DBHQ@Zn//DBHQ@I2 full cell achieves an exceptional cycling stability of 50 000 cycles with 90.89% capacity retention at 4 A g−1, and an areal capacity of 2.74 mAh cm−2 for the pouch cell at a low negative‐to‐positive (N/P) ratio of 4.04. This work establishes dual‐functional molecular layers as a versatile platform for stabilizing complex electrode interfaces, offering a new paradigm for addressing interdependent failure mechanisms in aqueous batteries.
nb5a4b4494943: Seawater electrolysis for green H2 production is hindered by the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and chloride corrosion at the anode. Although the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) can effectively reduce the overpotential, the sluggish mass transport of OH− at high current densities disrupts the oxygen release–regeneration balance, ultimately leading to a trade‐off between activity and stability. Here, we demonstrate that yttrium (Y) and carboxylate co‐doping reconstruct the interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network of NiFe oxyhydroxide, dynamically accelerating OH− delivery and enabling rapid regeneration of lattice oxygen. This catalyst maintains a high LOM contribution (51.7%–54%) while achieving exceptional durability and Cl− resistance. In situ Raman, differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS), and rotating ring‐disk electrode (RRDE) analyses confirm rapid peroxide intermediate formation, lattice oxygen participation, and negligible chlorine evolution. The anion‐exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzer delivers 1000 mA cm−2 at 1.79 V and operates stably for 800 h in alkaline seawater. This work establishes interfacial hydrogen‐bonding engineering as a generalizable strategy to break the activity–stability trade‐off for robust seawater electrolysis.
n2eba93c433d6: The bright promise of Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 as a next‐generation near‐room‐temperature thermoelectric material is challenged both by the need for reliable and economical synthesis and by performance degradation from detrimental Mg‐vacancy defects at grain boundaries and within grains. Here, we reveal that Earth‐abundant oxides (Fe2O3, ZrO2 and TiO2) can unlock superior thermoelectric performance in Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 via a simple metathesis strategy. Incorporation of the oxides (at only 1–3 mol%) in Mg‐excess Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 powders during spark‐plasma sintering initiates “Mg‐oxide” reduction reactions; the subsequent “transition metal‐Mg3(Sb,Bi)2” reactions release a source of additional Mg, whose global diffusion refills cationic vacancies in the bulk matrix, enabling markedly enhanced power factors and figures of merit. Our fabricated 8‐pair Mg3Sb0.75Bi1.25/MgAgSb device attained remarkable conversion efficiency and output power density of 11.7% and 1.0 W cm−2 at a temperature gradient (ΔT) of 315 K. Notably, a Mg3Sb0.5Bi1.5/Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 module demonstrated maximum cooling ΔTs competitive with state‑of‑the‑art Bi2Te3 coolers at 200–373 K. The proposed metathesis strategy not only offers an eco‐friendly and cost‐effective route to defect engineering, promoting applications of Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 TEs, but also provides key insights into the structure‐property relationships and thermoelectric performance optimization of other Mg‐based TEs and Zintl phases.
ne19ca393f88c: Alloying materials are promising anodes for high‐energy alkali‐ion batteries but suffer from rapid capacity fading. Here we demonstrate that tuning electrolyte‐anode interfacial reactivity enables ∼99% capacity retention of high‐loading bismuth anodes over 250 cycles in sodium‐ion batteries, whereas a highly reactive electrolyte results in rapid capacity decay to ∼20% within 10 cycles. Using bulk bismuth as a model system, we show that electrolyte interfacial reactivity critically governs anode pulverization and electrochemical stability by modulating grain refinement and the coupled evolution of particle cracking, electrode architecture, and solid‐electrolyte interphase (SEI) growth. Severe bismuth particle cracking and compositionally similar SEIs are observed in designed electrolytes of differing reactivities. A low‐reactivity electrolyte produces a porous electrode composed of micrometer‐sized bismuth grains coated with a thin SEI. In contrast, a high‐reactivity electrolyte drives pulverization into fine nanoparticles encapsulated by a thick SEI, yielding dense electrodes and fast capacity failure. This mechanism, further validated in Sn anodes for sodium‐ion batteries, is expected to be broadly applicable to large‐volume‐change alloying anodes, offering a general strategy for the development of next‐generation high‐energy alkali‐ion batteries.
nb95faae34bc0: Conventional self‐assembled hole‐transporting monolayers (SAMs) in perovskite solar cells (PSCs) suffer molecular aggregation, uneven coverage on rough FTO substrates, and insufficient interfacial defect passivation. The design and application of novel SAMs have become an important approach to enhancing device efficiency and stability. Herein, two asymmetric π‐extended SAMs, named T‐4PACz and FT‐4PACz, based on 4PACz skeleton with a triphenylamine terminal, were designed. FT‐4PACz, featuring a fused triphenylamine terminal, suppresses aggregation via moderate π–π stacking and adopts a parallel orientation on FTO, enhancing interfacial bonding and shortening carrier transport paths. Its exposed central nitrogen lone‐pair electrons strongly coordinate with Pb2+, passivating defects and regulating perovskite crystallization into dense, pinhole‐free films. Optimized HOMO alignment further reduces the hole‐injection barrier. Consequently, the champion inverted PSCs based on FT‐4PACz achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.76%, significantly outperforming those based on T‐4PACz (25.09%) and 4PACz (24.28%). The devices retain >90% of their initial efficiency after 1020 h at 85 °C in N2. This work provides a rational molecular design strategy for high‐performance, stable SAMs for PSCs.
n79370530e1e0: Complex degradation trajectories compromise the lifetime reliability and operational safety of lithium‐ion batteries in advanced energy‐storage systems. Aging pathways induced by temperature, rate, and voltage‐abuse stresses are often entangled in conventional health‐estimation models, limiting transferable degradation representation and future‐trajectory updating under distribution shifts. Here, a generalizable, mechanism‐anchored health‐management framework is developed for lithium‐ion batteries under heterogeneous aging conditions. Using aging‐condition identification as a proxy task, we identify a degradation‐sensitive 3.3–3.4 V charging window in LiFePO4/graphite cells, where statistically selected features are linked to incremental‐capacity fingerprints. These electrochemically anchored features are integrated with a condition‐aware soft mixture‐of‐experts model to disentangle heterogeneous feature–state‐of‐health (SOH) relationships with and without condition labels during inference. Cross‐dataset continual learning enables adaptation to an unseen data source while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Finally, data‐driven SOH observations are assimilated into a physics‐inspired parametric degradation model through an adaptive unscented Kalman filter, converting pointwise health estimates into online‐updatable degradation trajectories. The framework achieves robust SOH estimation across multi‐stress aging conditions and stable 100–300‐step look‐ahead trajectory prediction, establishing an interpretable route from electrochemical fingerprints to trajectory‐level battery prognostics.
n2699e10af151: Electrochemical urea synthesis via co-reduction of CO2 and nitrate (NO3 −) offers a sustainable route for C─N bond formation but remains challenged by poor selectivity and competing side reactions. Here, we report a dual-metal interfacial engineering strategy that enables C─N coupling by favoring a key NO─M1─NO─CO─M2 configuration. Using CuBi2O4 as a model precursor, in situ electroreduction induces reconstruction into an electron-enriched and low-coordinated Cu─Bi interfacial structure. Operando Raman and surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy, together with density functional theory calculations, reveal that these reconstructed dual-metal interfaces enable cooperative adsorption of NO3 − and CO2, favoring a spatially confined NO─Cu─NO─CO─Bi configuration. This proposed configuration lowers the overall activation barrier and converts the traditionally endergonic C─N coupling into an exergonic N─C─N coupling process, thereby redirecting the reaction pathway toward urea formation while suppressing nitrite and CO byproducts. As a result, the catalyst achieves a urea Faradaic efficiency of 32.7% at −0.4 V vs. RHE with a high yield rate of 2955.3 mg h−1 g−1 at −0.6 V vs. RHE under large current densities. This work provides insights into a generalizable interfacial-site design for modulating reaction pathways in electrosynthetic C─N coupling systems.
n9118b49e89e7: Electrochemical and photochemical carbon dioxide reduction reactions (CO2RR) represent pivotal strategies for converting CO2 into valuable chemicals, yet their multistep pathways and transient intermediates complicate the identification of the rate‐determining step (RDS). Kinetic isotope effects (KIEs) provide bond‐sensitive evidence by revealing how isotopic substitution changes reaction rates. This Perspective critically examines the application of KIEs to investigate CO2 activation, C─H bond formation, C─C coupling, water activation, and interfacial hydrogen transfer. Across these processes, normal, inverse, and near‐unity KIEs, when combined with spectroscopy and theoretical calculations, help distinguish competing elementary steps and reaction pathways. Isotope‐dependent product abundances further differentiate Langmuir–Hinshelwood and Eley–Rideal hydrogen transfer pathways and reveal how catalyst structure and interfacial environments regulate reaction pathways and selectivity. Finally, we discuss advances in isotope‐resolved operando detection, broader application of isotope analysis, and closer integration with theoretical calculations as opportunities to strengthen mechanistic analysis of CO2RR.
na4b1244d872f: Lithium‐rich manganese‐based oxides (LRMO) derive high capacity from lattice‐oxygen redox, but oxygen release at high voltage oxidizes solid electrolytes and drives rapid interfacial resistance growth. Nanosizing improves solid‐state kinetics yet exposes more under‐coordinated surface oxygen, aggravating interfacial degradation. Here, density functional theory screening identifies phosphate as the most effective oxyanion motif for stabilizing surface oxygen. Guided by this insight, a Li─P─F─O bonding topology is constructed through a one‐step mechanochemical reaction between LRMO and LiPO2F2. This process simultaneously refines the particles, introduces near‐surface fluorine, and forms a conformal amorphous interphase featuring P─O, P─F, and Li─F bonding environments. P–O coordination stabilizes surface oxygen, delocalizes oxidation holes, and suppresses O─O coupling, while near‐surface fluorine widens the Li layers and facilitates Li+ transport. Together, these effects suppress oxygen loss, electrolyte oxidation, impedance growth, and interfacial contact failure. The modified cathode delivers 248.5 mAh g−1 at 25°C and 268 mAh g−1 at 60°C (0.1 C), retains 85% capacity after 2000 cycles at 10 C, and operates up to 16 000 cycles. A high‐loading lithium‐metal pouch cell achieves 212 mAh g−1 with specific energy of 277 Wh kg−1. This work demonstrates bonding‐topology regulation as an effective strategy for stabilizing oxygen redox in solid‐state batteries.
n3b35f57e7e8b: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have achieved remarkable power conversion efficiency (PCE) recently, yet the device instability induced by defects remains a bottleneck. Despite the effectiveness of passivation strategies in reducing defects, conventional solution‐based methods may compromise the perovskite crystallinity. Thus, vapor‐based molecules are expected to penetrate into crystals and reduce defects. Screening effective vapor‐assisted passivation materials usually takes substantial trial‐and‐error costs. Here, we propose a hybrid workflow integrating machine learning models with first‐principles calculations to screen the key functional groups for vapor‐assisted passivation molecules and provide physical insights. The phenyl and halogen atoms were identified by Shapley additive explanation (SHAP) analysis to be effective. Theoretical calculations also indicated that there was a strong cation‐π interaction between Pb2+ and benzene ring. Besides, halogenated benzene could intercalate into the iodine vacancies on perovskite surfaces. Such robust interactions synergistically contribute to the stability of [PbI6]4− octahedral framework, and thus the formation of defects and structural collapse could be effectively suppressed. Moreover, the thermal conductivity of modified perovskite films was remarkably enhanced. Finally, the device modified with iodobenzene vapor achieved the champion PCE of 26.94%. This workflow integrating data‐driven discovery and atomistic understandings, provides an innovative strategy to screen vapor‐assisted passivation materials.
n2cff4d8a591b: Despite their high ionic conductivities, sulfide solid‐state electrolytes (SSEs) must reconcile ionic conductivity with mechanical integrity for ultrathin membrane fabrication when integrated into all‐solid‐state lithium metal batteries (ASSLMBs). This study reports a controllable 30 µm sandwich‑structured sulfide SSE membrane, fabricated by hot‑calendaring two Li5.3PS4.3ClBr0.7 (LPSClBr) membranes with a poly(vinylidene fluoride‑co‑hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF‑HFP) electrospun scaffold embedded with KH‑792‑modified Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP@KH) nanoparticles. PVDF‑HFP network accommodates electrode volume changes, while LATP@KH nanofillers serve as fast‐ion‐conducting bridges and fill grain boundaries to suppress lithium nucleation. First‐principles calculations reveal LATP's high density of states at Fermi level (57.10), enabling a Ti4+/Ti3+ redox reaction that in situ depletes infiltrating dendrites. The membrane achieves an ionic conductivity of 2.75 mS cm−1 and a critical current density of 1.0 mA cm−2. Li symmetric cells cycle stably for over 2000 h at 0.2 mA cm−2. LiIn||NCM811 full cells deliver 166.15 mAh g−1 at 0.2C (99.8% retention after 300 cycles) and exhibit negligible decay over 1000 cycles at 1C with ∼100% Coulombic efficiency. This work establishes a fast‐ion‐conductor‐modified polymer‐fiber composite architecture for mechanical reinforcement, in situ dendrite depletion and fast ion transport, offering a key design strategy for reliable ASSLMBs.
n077694b61ebd: The performance of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) remains critically dependent on the quality of the perovskite absorber, which is largely established during the antisolvent‐assisted crystallization process. Single‐antisolvent engineering, however, is often constrained by the fixed physicochemical properties of the chosen solvent, leaving limited flexibility to balance solvent extraction, crystallization modulation, and defect suppression. Herein, we report a physicochemical‐property‐assisted binary‐antisolvent engineering for high‐efficiency inverted PSCs. A series of binary antisolvent combinations were screened by considering key solvent properties, among which the carbon disulfide/anisole (CS2:ANI) system delivered the best device performance. Comprehensive chemical, structural, and optical characterizations reveal that the CS2:ANI system enables a more coordinated crystallization process by regulating solvent removal and modifying the precursor environment through interactions between CS2‐derived C═N‐containing species and the Pb–I framework. The resulting perovskite films exhibit compact morphology, reduced residual stress, and suppressed defect‐assisted nonradiative recombination. The optimized inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.73% and a steady‐state output efficiency of 26.43%.
n6cad52672a33: Lithium-iodine batteries are hindered by the polyiodide shuttle effect, where conventional mitigation strategies face a fundamental trade-off between active material confinement and redox reversibility. Herein, we report a monolithic host-separator continuum that address this dilemma through spatially organized compartmentalization. The architecture integrates an oxidized sulfonated lignin-functionalized graphene aerogel (GA@SOL) core with an encapsulating sulfonated cellulose polymer (SCP) shell via sequential infiltration and freeze-drying, minimizing the interfacial discontinuities inherent in stacked configurations. Within the conductive scaffold, iodine adsorption spontaneously generates a mixed-valence iodine species (I−/I2/I3 −) via balanced Lewis acid-base interactions, establishing a redox-active environment that preserves electronic connectivity without compromising reaction kinetics. Concurrently, the sulfonate-rich SCP shell establishes an electrostatic Donnan barrier that selectively repels polyiodide anions while facilitating Li+ transport. The resulting GA@SOL-I2@SCP cathode delivers 252 mAh g−1 at 1 C with 89.6% retention over 1500 cycles, a Li+ transference number of 0.63, and mitigated self-discharge (76.1% capacity retention after 120 h). Operando spectroscopy and in situ impedance monitoring confirm sustained polyiodide accessibility and suppressed anode corrosion. This work demonstrates that structural continuity and mixed-valence-enabled charge transport can decouple confinement from kinetic penalty, offering a design framework for conversion-type energy storage systems plagued by soluble intermediates.
n66c5725a7625: The effect of electrolytes on battery cell performance is multifaceted, and it is difficult to isolate their impact on individual processes. Operando analysis of batteries is a powerful tool to investigate battery degradation mechanisms. By combining different techniques on the same cell a wider perspective can be opened and enables easier cross‐correlation. Here, we introduce a fully laboratory‐based multimodal operando platform that synchronizes EIS/DRT, Raman spectroscopy, UV–vis reflectance spectroscopy, temperature monitoring, and galvanostatic cycling in one sealed Li–S cell. The platform is demonstrated over an extended observation window of up to 20 cycles to compare electrolyte‐dependent polysulfide speciation, transport limitations, and resistance evolution. The experimental design is optimized for reproducible mechanistic characterization and is not intended as a benchmark of practical cell performance or long‐term cycle life.
n9d88cf80f357: Adaptive thermal‐management materials capable of direction‐dependent heat transport are highly desirable for building‐envelope and other moderate‐temperature applications, yet scalable and flexible thermal rectifiers remain limited. Here, we report a polyester‐based phase‐change thermal diode meta‐fabric (TDMF) fabricated via continuous modified rotary jet spinning (M‐RJS), with potential compatibility for textile‐scale processing. The TDMF comprises a hot‐pressed reduced graphene oxide (rGO)‐integrated dense conductive layer (DCL) and an ultra‐porous fluffy insulating layer (FIL), coupling structural asymmetry with phase‐change‐induced thermal nonlinearity.
